rows.original: Just who is she and what was she doing out in the tunnels alone?
rows.translation: 她究竟是谁？为什么会独自在隧道里？
rows.raw: "Just who is she and what was she doing out in the tunnels alone?"

rows.original:
"We're a people who exhibit elemental affinities, much like many others around the world. Met a galepup sailor once, big and boisterous, too rich for my blood. You can see these — " she points up to her goo-like hair and ears, then down at her similarly gooey tails and the swirling patterns on her skin — "for what they are, but otherwise I'm really not that different from you."
        
        [party.has atugia
            |"Oh, so they aren't runes," Atugia says. "When I first saw the symbols on you I thought they might've been, but appearances are deceiving, aren't they?"
            |To be fair, that's a little like saying horses and chickens aren't really that different from each other just because they've got heads, eyes and legs. Most people don't have glowing patterns over more than half their bodies, for one.
        ]
        
        Nihara laughs. "I was born with them, like my parents and all others of my kind. There's no point in wondering what I could've been when I'm fine as I am. But yes, I can't help but love water. I'm not going to bore you with my history and it's rather improper to dump your life story on someone that you've just met, so let's leave it at I'm just another person like you and me who can do a few fancy things with water, that's all. Not that much from a wizard who might've learned a few parlor tricks to do the same."
        
        You get the feeling that she's downplaying the topic, evading the point and understating the matter without being outright untruthful, but pressing her right now is likely to be counterproductive. Maybe later...
rows.translation:
我们和世界上许多其他民族一样，都具有与某些自然元素相呼应的特质。我曾经遇到过一位来自盖勒普群岛的水手，他身材高大、性格豪爽，财富也远超我的想象。你可以从这些——”她指着自己那黏稠状的头发和耳朵，又指了指同样黏稠的尾巴以及皮肤上那些螺旋状的纹路——“看出我们的不同之处，但除此之外，我和你们其实并没有什么区别。
        
        [party.has atugia
            |哦，原来这些并不是符文啊，”阿图吉娅说道。“当我第一次看到你身上的那些符号时，我还以为它们可能是符文呢，不过外表有时候确实会骗人，不是吗？
            |公平地说，这就好比因为马和鸡都有头、眼睛和腿，就认为它们其实并没有什么区别。毕竟，大多数人的身体上并没有超过一半的部分会闪烁着光芒。
        ]
        
        尼原笑了起来：“我和我的父母，以及我们这一族的其他人一样，生来就具备这种能力。既然我现在这样很好，再去思考自己本来可能会变成什么样子，也没有意义吧。不过，我确实无法抗拒对水的喜爱。我不想用我的经历来烦扰你，而且把自己的生活故事告诉一个刚认识的人，也确实有些不妥。所以，我们就这么说吧——我只不过是一个和你一样，能够利用水做出一些奇妙事情的人而已，仅此而已。 对于一个或许只是学会了一些花招就能做到同样的事情的巫师来说，这也算不了什么吧。”

你会觉得她在淡化这个话题，回避重点，轻描淡写地描述这件事，但同时又没有完全说谎。不过，现在逼她继续谈论这个话题，反而可能会适得其反。 也许稍后吧……

rows.original: What is one of these water wyrd things, anyway?
rows.translation: 这些水灵相关的物品，到底是什么呢？
rows.raw: "What is one of these water wyrd things, anyway?"

rows.original:
"Well... I was. Not anymore, given that it's in ruins now and most everyone fled to the sanctuary of the pantheon in Khor'minos. I lived there when I was young, but chose to move to this side of the lake after I reached my majority in order to be closer to the people I served. Nevertheless, the temple's not that far away, and there used to be a whole bunch of regular ferry services over the lake in the event that I didn't want to swim; I'd check in with the sister at the temple once or twice every week."
        
        Ah. What did she use to do here? Judging from what you saw on your way in, you'd gather that this is some kind of spa?
        
        "Not that the people still out here are willing to leave the walls of their villas to come to me, but in a sense, yes. To say that I'm a healer would be to imply that I bind wounds and cure diseases, which while I can do, is not my trade; what happens here is more a cleansing of the body through the curative aspect of water. A purging of toxins, as it were — minoan patricians enter the city on business, breathe the filthy, crowded air, are exposed to all manner of poisons that originate from so many people living in so small a space, and participate in all manner of social events that has them ingesting rich foods and the like. Little wonder that they flee for their rural villas once the king's court is out of session. When they return, they come to me and I remove those accumulated dregs from their body and soul alike. Massages, hydration, cold baths — now that I am to go to them these days instead of the other way around, I can only do so much, but it's still better than nothing."
        
        [party.has cait
            |"I know what she's talking about," Cait pipes up. "That kind of therapy is pretty popular in Jassira and Tronarii."
            
            You'd be surprised if it weren't — in desert nations like those, it would be considered a tremendous waste of water and hence a convenient way to flaunt one's wealth. But yeah, it's not as if you thought Nihara wasn't legit to begin with.
            |By the looks of her things, so many of them are minotaur-sized — she must have been doing a brisk business before all this started.
        ]
        
        "I was indeed living quite comfortably off what the patricians were paying me, with enough to spare to make rather generous tithes back to the temple as a good sister doing outreach work. But as you can see, that's come to an abrupt halt. Not as if money's going to do you much good when there's nothing to buy with it."
        
        Nihara looks a little melancholy at the thought, then shakes it off. "Well then, I hope that brief explanation was enough. If you'd like a demonstration, I'm sure that can be arranged later for a suitable price. Not in money, not these days..."
rows.translation:
嗯……我曾经住在那里。但现在那里已经变成废墟了，几乎所有人都逃到了科尔米诺斯的七神避难所。我年轻时曾在那里生活，但成年后为了能更接近我服务的人们，便搬到了湖的这一边。不过，那座神庙其实并不远，以前如果我不想游泳的话，湖上还有许多定期的渡轮服务。我每周都会去神庙那里看望一次那位修女。
        
        啊，她之前是用来做些什么的？从你进来时看到的情况来看，应该这里是一种水疗中心吧？

“虽然现在还留在这里的人们并不愿意走出他们的别墅来见我，但从某种意义上来说，确实可以这么认为。 如果说我是一名治疗者，那意味着我能够治愈伤势、消除疾病。虽然我确实具备这样的能力，但这并非我的主要职责。实际上，我所做的更多是通过水这种具有治愈作用的力量来净化身体，清除体内的毒素。可以这么说，米诺斯贵族们因公务来到这座城市，呼吸着污浊而拥挤的空气，接触到由于众多人生活在狭小的空间里而产生的各种毒素，同时还要参加各种各样的社交活动，导致他们摄入大量的高热量食物等等。因此，我所做的其实就是帮助他们的身体摆脱这些有害物质的干扰。 难怪每当国王的宫廷会议结束，他们就会赶往乡下的别墅去。当他们回来时，就会来找我，而我则会帮助他们清除那些积聚在他们身体和心灵中的污垢。按摩、补水、冷水浴——这些这些天是我去照顾他们，而不是他们来照顾我，所以我能做的有限，但总比什么都不做好吧。"
        
        [party.has cait
            |我知道她在说什么，”凯特插话说，“那种疗法在贾西拉和特罗纳里相当流行。”

其实这也难怪——在那些沙漠国家，这种做法会被认为是一种极其浪费水资源的做法，因此也就成了人们炫耀财富的一种方式。不过，说实在的，你本来也就不会认为尼哈拉的做法有什么不妥吧。
            |从她拥有的那些东西来看，其中有好多都是弥诺陶洛斯那么大的尺寸——在这一切发生之前，她肯定生意非常红火。
        ]
        
        依靠贵族们支付给我的报酬，我的生活确实过得相当舒适，甚至还有足够的钱作为一位热心公益的姐妹，向寺庙捐赠慷慨的什一税。但正如你们所见，这一切现在已经戛然而止了。 反正钱也没什么用处，买了东西也用不了。”

尼原想到这里，脸上浮现出一丝忧郁，但很快又将其甩掉了。“那么，希望我的这个简短解释已经足够了。 如果您想要看看演示效果，我相信稍后可以以一个合适的价格安排这次演示。当然，这里说的价格不是指金钱……至少现在不是指这个。

rows.original: Actually, you think you're done here. It's been a pleasure meeting her, but you've got to be on the road now. "Stay safe out there. While the patrols from the city do their best to beat back the imps, they can't be everywhere — and thank you for aiding me back there." Nihara beams. "It was fun and timely meeting you; why don't I see you to the door, [pc.name]? Come back anytime you feel like you need yourself cleaned up!" The azure goo-kitten rises from her seat and offers you her hand; she takes yours in a sisterly fashion and warmly leads you to the door. It's kind of funny how she's so easily slid into the demeanor of a protective elder sibling who's completely in charge of the situation when she was the one who needed saving mere moments ago, but you can see why her minotaur clientele would be appreciative of it. As you walk away, you take note of the lake house and the long bridge that leads to it from the sandy shore. You'll be able to return here anytime you like from here on.

|我在寺庙中长大，因为我的父母都是这种信仰的追随者。我也去过城市，见识过人们在那里的生活方式……可以说，我的成长环境相当优越，我没有像许多被关在笼子里的老鼠一样，被束缚在狭小的空间里。 在寺庙的外面，只有我、我的父母、女院长还有几位看管人……当然，还有那些死者。很多死者。 有些人可能会认为，住在离逝者安息之地不远处会对孩子不利，但她的成长似乎并没有受到影响。 如果你想享受生活，就不能害怕死亡，”尼原平静地回答道，“不，如果你真的想享受生活、珍惜他人，就绝对不能害怕死亡。分离只是我们为了暂时相聚而必须付出的代价，而即便如此，这种相聚也终究是短暂的。 你不能因为害怕受伤而不敢去尝试。 |她一个人待在湖中央，会不会感到孤独呢？每当你不在她身边、无法陪在她身边的时候，你确实会感到担心。 “嗯，你完全不需要为我担心，”尼哈拉一边说，一边向你飞了一个吻。“想要让我陷入困境，需要的可不只是那么几个小妖精啊。就像我之前说的，还有很多人都躲在他们的别墅里，即使在这种时候——不， 尤其是 在这种时候——我必须为他们挺身而出。所以，如果你担心我会变得孤僻封闭，那你完全没必要担心。正是这样的时刻，才能真正看出谁是真正彼此关心、相互扶持的人，而谁又会为了寻求安全而抛弃他人，逃往科尔米诺斯的城墙后面。 看到如今这片沙质湖岸变得如此空旷，与过去的景象相比确实让人感到有些难过，但那些留下来的人们之间的感情却变得更加深厚了。 是啊，你只是担心她要照顾所有人，但谁又会来照顾她呢？ 她 那么，当更艰难的时刻来临时该怎么办呢？ 尼原翻了个白眼，但还是笑了起来：“如果你真的这么坚决地想要为我做这件事，那么这难道就是你想听到的答案吗？” 嗯，其实也并没有什么确切的答案…… 通缉中 听起来还可以，这样就挺好。 |她的父母现在还在……嗯，还在身边吗？如果他们是水族，他们也不可能像尼哈拉自己一样，因为某些原因而无法躲进科尔米诺斯。现在她孤身一人在这里。如果我的问题问得太过冒昧，还请见谅，但是…… 哦不，不，他们没事的。爸爸妈妈是在大约半年前被叫回特罗纳里的，就在这一切开始之前；应该是妈妈那边的家族继承问题吧。他们本来打算等事情处理完毕后再回来，但横跨大洋需要好几周的时间，而我也没机会去探望他们的情况。 我最后一次见到他们的时候，他们身体健康，一切都很好。不过已经过去半年了，没有任何消息，无论是好消息还是坏消息。 听到这个消息真是太好了。也许这算是一种不祥的预兆吧，但在你的旅途中，你遇到的很多人，要么从来不知道自己的父母是谁，要么已经失去了父母，又或者根本没人提起过这个话题。 也许等他们回来的时候，这一切混乱都已经得到解决，他们就可以专心去夺回蒂拉神庙了。 “那当然很好，但我也不会过分依赖女神的庇佑。 俗话说，长时间把一个人扛在肩上会让她感到疲惫不堪。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |Was she born here? In the undermountain, by the great city of the minotaurs? "Well, no, but I may as well have been. I was born in Tronarii, but it was so long ago and I was so young that I don't even remember what it was like. My parents were part of a Tiran mission to support the temple that'd been founded here in the tunnels, so we came here. The faith isn't as hierarchical as the Jassiran Temple is, but there's still a sense of kinship; we're not like Sorran sects where a minor disagreement over what the goddess actually said causes them to splinter ever further. "Aanyways. I grew up in the temple just down in the tunnels and don't remember much of Tronarii, so there's really no difference between me and someone born and bred here, don't you think? Even after I came of age, there really hasn't been much reason for me to leave the mountain — while I do love the moon, I haven't seen it for a while, and to be honest the glow of the lake is a lot prettier and closer to home to boot." Yeah. Given what she's just said, she really does think of this place as her home. "Home is where the heart is, [pc.name]. I don't have any heart for that shining city upon the hill, but here upon this lakeshore... well." |She mentioned that she would perform health services for the local minotaur patricians in the area, right? Massages, spas, and other things like that? Nihara nods. "Mostly water-based methods of detoxification, given there's a whole lake of it under our feet. Sanitation in Khor'minos proper is as good as it gets, but there's only so much that can be done when you've got so many people packed in one place even before the quarantine. Then there's the matter of the slums, which are absolutely filthy, and that filth inevitably spills over into the streets of the other districts. The patricians used to go into the city on government business or to enjoy the circuses, then flee straight back for the healthier and more pleasant environment of their villas. That's where I come in, scrubbing the filth from their bodies both inside and out." You've seen some of the villas on your way in — even when abandoned, they're still quite the luxurious sight. She must've been well-paid for her services, given that the people living in them must've been creatures of comfort. "There're still a couple around who're still out here, who returned from Khor'minos that the inner city's been infiltrated by the demons and they'd rather take their chances behind their own walls. I don't know how true that is, but so long as they're out here I go tend to them, although it's less pleasure and more triage these days." |"Is it so strange that I'm a water wyrd? There're plenty of peoples out there who've some connection to the primordial elements and spirits like hellhounds and galehounds... I don't consider myself any stranger for being able to do what I do any more than a cowgirl is particularly good at giving milk." What can she do, anyway? "Swim well. Not drown. Have hair like mine. I have to live near open water and can't leave it for too long, or else I dry out. Oh, and absorb fluid — not just water — from my markings or hair, or, uh, any other way most other peoples do." She coughs a bit, trying to be surreptitious about what she's trying to say without outright saying it. "See? Not so weird." Ah, right. You can see how her services would've been popular amongst the minotaurs, and why her priestess' outfit is skimpy enough to rival Cait's. "We-ll... it's simply part of the service, you know? Drawing out their bodily humors so they can be properly cleansed?" Sure, sure... "Sure, sometimes people who come to me for the first time get a little spooked, but it quickly passes when they learn that I mean them no harm." She flutters her eyelashes at you[nihara.isCorrupted | |, but just manages to look more awkward than coquettish ]. "Do I look like the horrid kind of girl who'd do that?" |"I was raised in the temple, given that my parents were adherents to the faith. I've been to the city and seen how people live there... I'd say that I was fairly privileged in my upbringing to not be squeezed into a tiny space like so many rats in cages. Out by the temple, it was just me, my parents, the mother superior and a couple more caretakers... and of course, the dead. A lot of the dead." Some people might consider living not too far away from the final resting place of people detrimental to a child, but she seems to have turned out well. "You can't be afraid of death if you're going to enjoy life," Nihara replies flatly. "No, you can't be afraid of death if you want to truly enjoy life and others. A parting's the price we pay to be together for a while, and even then it doesn't last. You can't be afraid to reach out for fear of being burned." |Does she get lonely, out here by herself in the middle of the lake? In all the times when you're not here to be able to be with her, you do worry. "Well, you don't need to worry about me in the least," Nihara replies, blowing you a kiss. "It'll take more than a couple of imps to keep me down, so there's that. Like I've told you, there're still a bunch of people holed up in their villas, and even in these times — no, especially in these times — I've got to be out there for them. So if you're worried about me being a shut-in, there's absolutely no reason for you to fret. It's at times like this when you know who's really dedicated to each other and who's going to just break, cut and run to the safety of Khor'minos' walls. It's a little sad seeing the sandy lakeshore so empty compared to what it once used to be, but the bonds between those who remain grow stronger." Yeah, you know. You're just worried because she has to play nursemaid to everyone, but who's going to play nursemaid for her when tougher times arrive? Nihara rolls her eyes, but smiles. "You, if you're so determined to do it for me. Is that the answer you wanted to hear?" Well, there wasn't exactly an answer you wanted to hear, but that'll do just fine. |Are her parents still... well, around? If they were water wyrds they couldn't have taken refuge inside Khor'minos for the same reasons Nihara herself can't, and she's all alone here. You're sorry if this is prying a little too far, but — "Oh no, no, they're fine. Mom and Dad just got called back to Tronarii about a half-year ago, before all this started; something about inheritance on Mom's side of the family, I believe. They were supposed to come back when their business was concluded, but it can take weeks to cross the ocean and well, I haven't really had the opportunity to head out and ask about them. The last time I saw them they were healthy and fine, but it's been a half-year. No news, good or bad." That's great to hear. Maybe it's some kind of ill omen or something, but so many people you've met on your travels either never knew their parents, lost them, or the subject was never brought up. Maybe by the time they do return all this mess will have been cleaned up and they can focus on taking back the temple of Tira. "That'd be lovely, but I'm not going to lean too much on the goddess' blessings. Carrying a single person on her shoulders for too long tires her out, as the saying goes." ] "

rows.original: [rand |"Tira is most commonly known as the goddess of death and time — " she points to the hourglass clasp holding her black-and-gold garments together — "but she's also the patron of soldiers and kings, as well as that of nations and empires. Of all the Seven, she's got what's arguably the biggest and most diverse official portfolio. When you look at how people in different parts of the world revere the divines in their own way, there're often local idiosyncrasies to be had, such as how Keros is considered to have domain over agriculture in the far east, while sailors also tend to attribute not just storms, but governance of the sea itself to Sorra." [pc.bg acolyte |Yeah, not uncommon at all — it was a topic you'd come to be fairly familiar with in the course of your studies as an acolyte. Most people aren't aware of all the little details of local worship, although most do know that different peoples have their own interpretations of the gods' appearances |Now that's an interesting approach. You'd known that different peoples have had their own interpretations of the gods, but the differences were cosmetic and superficial at best ]. "Just because she's the goddess of death doesn't mean there's any need to fear her," Nihara continues. "She makes sure that the threads of our fates are cut at their appointed times — not before, and not after. Her followers are tasked with removing the lingering dead from this world and to end their suffering. She's reasonable, if you can convince her that it's necessary for her to stay her hand, if the need is great enough, she will; people have talked her into it before. There's a difference between a ceremonious ending... and otherwise." |Why is there a Tiran temple all the way out in the tunnels, anyway? As you understand it, there's a serviceable pantheon in Khor'minos proper where her colleagues took refuge in. "Well, the city is big, and space is at a premium — above, below and around. Given how many people there are in those walls, we wouldn't have the space to inter all of them. When you're a devotee of the goddess of death, you're made aware of just how many people pass in a day free of foul play, and conversely, how many people must be born in that same time. "That temple was originally founded with the help of the minotaur king of the time in order to use some of the old mining tunnels to lay the people of the city to their final rest, you understand. They were just there and empty, so he thought it'd be good to fill them up... these days, only the wealthy are capable of affording a spot in the city's catacombs proper, but some of the patricians opted to be buried near their country villas. That's... or rather, was, another of my jobs." You see. Nihara sighs. "My biggest concern, really, is that the goos that invaded the temple have tainted the corpses. Or even worse, the other way around. Normally, I'd be confident about the wards holding, but given the corruption's run so deep anything's possible at this point." |"I was never very much associated with the whole psychopomp aspect of the Tiran faith — as someone who was supposed to do outreach, the most I'd do was to prepare the initial rites if someone happened to pass away in the lakeshore district. Put them in gentle repose, then send for someone from the temple to take them away for the cremation, embalming, or however the family wanted the body disposed of before what was left got interred in the tunnels by the temple." The rites, huh... "People here aren't like Jassirans or Tronarrians, they're not that big into bringing their wealth with them into the next life and instead leaving their material things for their living issue to enjoy. What most of the Tiran rites about these parts did was to make sure the bones and other remains of people weren't stolen." Ugh.[pc.bg arcanist acolyte scholar | You have some idea of what they'd be wanted for. Nihara nods | Who would want to steal such things? Nihara sighs ]. "Those who would be looking for the remains of say, ancient minotaur kings or the great mothers to use in so-called enchanting, the same way you'd use a piece of a dragon to imbue an echo of its spirit into something valuable to you. As you can imagine, there've been several scandals of this sort before, which is why the minoan royalty personally took an interest in funding the temple out there in the tunnels. In wilder places like Valgarde, the people there take it a step further, considering it customary to cannibalize bites out of the glorious deceased in the hopes that they would get the traits of the dead. Tirans were instrumental in putting a stop to such barbaric practices that spread diseases, amongst other things. "But that's all beyond me. I'm just here to help people not fear the reaper so much, and make sure they're in tip-top shape for when she does call to them." |"We've never really had a big presence in this region — it used to be almost all Lumian primacy from the Greyvales up to the eastern coast, or at least that's what I was told. The pantheon in Khor'minos is mostly perfunctory when it comes to a bunch of the deities, with their statues being there just to be there. "But that's fine. Having fewer of us around just means that each one of us is more special, and we were never swamped or understaffed to begin with. Because I'm the only one to live out over the lake like this, it used to be that almost everyone in the patricians' villas and along the shore knew my face and called me by name. That felt really nice, I'll admit." |"Heheheh. You like my outfit, don't you? It's quite obvious, when I feel your eyes on me." Well, it is very eye-catching. If you didn't know better and it weren't for the obvious symbology, you'd have imagined it was some kind of exotic Mallachite get-up. Nihara tsks, wagging a finger in your direction. "Yes, yes, and I'm sure Lumians all uniformly wrap themselves from head to toe in body bags with only the eyes peeking out. Fact is that Mallach isn't the only one who understands the basics of good appeal, and since I was supposed to be face of the temple to the public as it were, I decided to play to my strengths. Being all shrouded and intimidating does have its own mystique, but it's not really the one you want to present when you're trying to convince others that your goddess is an approachable part of daily life." By showing off plenty of skin. "Hey, my skin needs to breathe, and I've got to be able to move freely while wearing all of this, swimming included. A girl like me's got needs, you know. But no. If it helps, I'm not the one who came up with this design — it's actually fairly commonplace back in Tronarii, I hear. Of course, since I've never been back there, I wouldn't be able to say for sure, but I don't see any reason to disbelieve it." |Did the local minotaurs always have the habit of interring their dead? Did it come with the Tiran faith here? The temple you passed by on the way to the city was old, but it still looked far newer than the adjoining tunnels. "Oh, no. While the burial tunnels adjoining the temple are old and the catacombs under Khor'minos even older, the practice of the minotaurs burying their dead like this predates their coming to believe in the seven divines. Although the Tirans did put a stop to many of the most cruel and barbaric practices, we accommodated as many of the more reasonable customs into the faith as possible, so long as they did not contravene the goddess' teachings." So it was an ancient minoan custom. Nihara taps her chin, looking thoughtful. "I believe so. Local legend has it that before the seven divines came to be known in this part of the world, a terrible giant of primordial earth and flame dwelled beneath this very mountain. It had developed quite a taste for the flesh of sapient beings, you see, and so flaming chasms were a common occurrence upon the mountains and the adjoining foothills and coast — opening in the blink of an eye to swallow the hapless and closing up again just as quickly." [flags.FIRE_TEMPLE |Come to think of it... you remember the temple of terrestrial fire back in the Frostwood. Was there any relation to this primordial being? Nihara shrugs. "I don't know what temple you speak of, but the peoples of this corner of the world used to worship many animistic spirits. It may be possible that the two are connected, it may be not, the minoan legends don't say. |That sounds pretty horrific, and yet it makes sense that the ancient minotaurs would revere such a being — out of fear, if nothing else. "Primordial beings and animistic spirits commanded a more... diverse approach to matters than the seven divines, [pc.name]. More unknowable and capricious, as befits a time of chaos lost to the earliest myths and legends. ] "Either way, a minotaur chieftain of the time discovered that his bride-to-be was slated to be the giant's next meal. The details are scant, but given the considerable motivation present he confronted the primordial being and managed to work out a deal: it would allow the people of the lands it dwelled under to live in relative peace, and in return every single being in the chieftain's domain, minotaur or otherwise, would be fed to the earth when they passed so the giant could feast upon all the flesh of the multitudes that could prosper upon a peaceful land. "The giant was a being of innate fire and endless hunger, but had enough greed in it to understand the concept of delayed gratification; there was sense in staying its hand for the moment so it could have more flesh later. The deal was struck, and the quakes, crevasses and lavaspouts stopped as long as the minotaurs interred the dead of all who dwelled in their expanding kingdom." The way she tells it, there's more to the story, though. "You're right. Unbeknownst to the giant, the minotaur chief and his bride fashioned a charm into their agreement with the monster, a charm that would take centuries beyond their deaths to complete as each generation of their kin so consumed fed fragments of their own power into it. But when it was completed, the giant was bound beneath the mountain far below our feet, the only trace of it today being the burning crystals that Khor'minos uses as lights. Blood of the mountain, they call it, as it's supposedly droplets of the giant's blood as it seeps to the surface. "Now, no more flesh is fed to the monster, and bones lie in quiet repose within the temple ossuary and catacombs in honor of the goddess of death. But the minotaurs continue to bury their dead anyway, and we Tirans are happy to ease them through that burden." ]
rows.translation: [rand |提拉通常被认为是死亡与时间的女神——”她指着那条将她的黑金服饰固定在一起的沙漏形饰物说道，“但她同时也是士兵与国王的庇护者，更是各个国家与帝国的守护神。 在七位神明之中，她无疑拥有最为庞大且最为多样化的官方形象体系。当你观察世界各地的人们是如何以各自的方式崇敬这些神明时，往往会发现一些地方性的特点：例如，在远东地区，人们认为凯罗斯掌管着农业；而水手们则倾向于将风暴乃至整个海洋的秩序都归功于索拉。" [pc.bg acolyte |是的，这种情况其实相当普遍——在你作为学徒进行学习的过程中，这个话题会让你逐渐变得熟悉。大多数人并不了解当地宗教仪式中的那些细节，不过他们确实知道，不同的人群会对神灵的外貌有不同的解读。 |这个方法确实很有意思。你早就知道，不同民族对神灵有着各自的诠释，但这些差异充其量也只是表面上的、形式上的而已。 ]仅仅因为她是死亡女神，并不意味着我们就应该害怕她，”尼哈拉继续说道，“她只是确保我们的命运之线在预定的时间被切断——既不会提前，也不会推迟。 她的追随者们肩负着将那些滞留在这个世界中的死者从世上带走、终结他们痛苦的重任。她是个通情达理的人，只要你能说服她，让她相信有必要保持克制，而当这种需求足够迫切时，她就会听从劝告的——以前也有人成功说服她这么做的。 有一个正式的结局……和其他的结局之间是有区别的。 |为什么在隧道的最深处会有提兰的神庙呢？你知道的，在科尔米诺斯城内本身就有可供使用的神殿，她的同事们也是在那里避难的。 “嗯，这座城市很大，空间非常紧张——无论是地上、地下还是其他地方，空间都非常有限。 考虑到那些围墙里面住着那么多人，我们根本没有足够的空间来安置他们所有人。当你成为死亡女神的信徒之后，你就会意识到：每天有多少人是在没有遭遇任何不幸的情况下离世的，而与此同时，又必须有同样多的人诞生出来。 那座寺庙最初是在当时弥诺陶洛斯国王的帮助下建立的，目的是利用一些古老的采矿隧道来安葬这座城市的人们，你明白我的意思吧。那些隧道原本是空的，所以国王认为把它们填满会是个好主意。这些天来，只有富人才有能力在城市的地下墓穴中安葬自己，但有些贵族却选择将亲人安葬在他们的乡间别墅附近。这也是……或者说，曾经是我的工作之一。 你瞧。 尼哈拉叹了口气：“说真的，我最担心的是那些侵入寺庙的怪物把尸体污染了。或者更糟糕的是，情况恰恰相反。通常情况下，我对这些防护措施很有信心，但鉴于这种污染已经如此严重，现在什么情况都可能发生。" |我其实从来都不是提兰信仰中那些与‘引导灵魂’相关的仪式活动的积极参与者。作为负责这些外联工作的人，我最多也就是在湖滨地区有人去世时，帮忙准备一些最初的仪式而已。 将他们安放好，然后派人去寺庙，将他们的遗体移走，进行火化、防腐处理，或者按照家属的意愿处理遗体，之后再将剩余的部分安葬在寺庙附近的隧道里。这些仪式啊…… “这里的人们和贾西兰人或特罗纳里安人不一样，他们并不那么看重将财富带往来世，而是会把这些物质财富留給自己的后代去享用。 蒂兰人针对这些部位所采取的措施，主要是为了确保人们的骨骼及其他遗骸不会被盗走。 呃……[pc.bg arcanist acolyte scholar | 你应该大概知道他们为什么会被人通缉吧。 西原点了点头。 | 谁会想要偷这样的东西呢？ 西原叹了口气。 ]那些想要寻找古代弥诺陶洛斯国王的遗骸，或者那些被称为‘伟大母亲’的神秘存在的人，其实都是想利用这些遗骸来施展所谓的魔法。就像你会利用龙的一块骨头，让它的精神融入到你珍视的物品之中一样。 可以想象，此前已经发生过好几起这样的丑闻，正因为如此，米诺斯王室才亲自出钱资助在隧道中建造的那座神庙。而在像瓦尔加德这样的偏远地区，人们甚至走得更远——他们认为，食用逝者的肉体是一种传统习俗，这样就能获得逝者的特质。 暴君们在制止这些会传播疾病等恶劣行为方面发挥了重要作用。 “但这些事情已经超出了我的能力范围。我在这里只是为了帮助人们减少对死神的恐惧，确保他们在死神降临的时候能够处于最佳状态。" |我们在这个地区其实从未真正拥有过强大的影响力——从格雷瓦莱斯一直到东海岸，这一地区几乎一直都是由卢米安人主导的，至少我是这么听说的。在科尔米诺斯，很多神祇的存在其实只是象征性的，他们的雕像只是被摆在那里而已。 不过这也没关系。我们的人数减少了，反而意味着每个人都会变得更加重要。而且我们本来就从未面临过人手不足的问题。因为我是唯一一个住在湖对岸的人，所以以前贵族们的别墅里以及沿岸的居民几乎都知道我的面孔，还会直接叫我的名字。 我得承认，那种感觉真的很棒。 |嘿嘿嘿，你喜欢我的装扮，对吧？当我感觉到你在看我的时候，这一点就很明显了。” 嗯，确实是这样。 是 非常醒目。如果你不了解内情，再加上那些明显的象征符号，你肯定会以为这是某种异国情调的玛拉基特服饰呢。 尼哈拉轻笑着，朝你的方向摇着手指：“没错，没错，我敢肯定卢米安人都是从头到足部裹着尸袋，只让眼睛露在外面呢。 事实上，了解如何吸引人们注意力的基本要素的人并不只有马拉克。既然我某种程度上应该成为这座神庙在公众面前的代表，我就决定发挥自己的优势。虽然全身笼罩在神秘的面纱中、给人一种威严的感觉确实会增添一些神秘感，但当你试图让别人相信你的女神是人们日常生活中可以亲近的存在时，这种形象其实并不适合。通过展示大量的肌肤来吸引注意力。 “嘿，我的肌肤需要…… 呼吸而且，穿着这些装备，我必须能够自由活动，包括游泳。像我这样的女孩，也有自己的需求，你懂的。但是，这个设计其实并不是我提出的——据我所知，在特洛纳里，这种设计其实相当常见。当然，因为我从未去过那里，所以也不能确定，但我觉得没有理由不相信这一点。 |当地的弥诺陶洛斯是否一直都有埋葬死者的习惯？这种习俗是不是与他们这里的提兰信仰有关？你在前往城市的路上经过的那座寺庙虽然很古老，但它看起来仍然比周围的隧道要新得多。 哦，不。虽然寺庙附近的埋葬隧道很古老，而科尔米诺斯地下的地下墓穴更为古老，但弥诺陶洛斯人以这种方式埋葬死者的习俗，其实早在他们开始信仰那七位神明之前就已经存在了。 尽管暴君们确实制止了许多最残酷、最野蛮的行为，但我们还是尽可能地将那些较为合理的习俗融入到了信仰之中，只要这些习俗不违背女神的教诲。这确实是一种古老的米诺斯习俗。 尼哈拉托着下巴，若有所思地说道：“我想是的。当地的传说记载，在这片土地上七位神明被人们所知晓之前，有一头由原始大地与火焰构成的恐怖巨兽居住在这座山的下面。 你看，它已经对智慧生物的肉体产生了极大的兴趣，因此，在那些山脉、邻近的山足部地带以及海岸线上，火焰深渊变得极为常见——它们会在瞬间出现，将那些不幸的生物吞没，然后同样迅速地闭合起来。" [flags.FIRE_TEMPLE |仔细想想……你还记得在霜林里的那座大地之火神庙吧？那个远古生物和它之间会不会有什么关联呢？ 尼哈拉耸了耸肩：“我不知道你说的那座神庙是什么，但这个世界的这个角落的人们过去常常崇拜许多自然精灵。这两者之间或许存在某种联系，也有可能没有关联，米诺斯的传说并没有提到这一点。 |那听起来确实非常可怕，不过也难怪古代的米诺陶人会敬畏这样的存在——至少是出于恐惧吧。 “原始生物与万物有灵论所信仰的精灵们，在处理各种事务时采取的方式，要比那七位神明更加……多样化。 [pc.name]更加不可预测、更加变幻莫测——这正是那个被最早的神话与传说所笼罩的混乱时代的应有面貌。 ] 无论如何，当时有一位弥诺陶洛斯部落的首领发现，他的未婚妻即将成为那头巨人的下一顿食物。关于这一事件的详细情况并不多，但鉴于首领有着强烈的动机，他最终与这个远古生物达成了一项协议：只要巨人在他领地范围内生活时能让当地居民们过上相对安宁的生活，那么首领领地内的所有生物——无论是弥诺陶洛斯还是其他种族——在死亡后都会被献给巨人，这样巨人就能享受到这片和平之地上的所有生物所提供的肉食。 那头巨兽本质上是充满火焰与无尽饥饿感的生物，但它也具备足够的贪婪之心，因此能够理解“延迟满足”的概念；它明白暂时克制自己的欲望，才能在未来获得更多的猎物。就这样，双方达成了协议：只要弥诺陶洛斯将他们不断扩张的领地内所有生物的尸体埋葬掉，地震、裂缝以及熔岩喷发就会停止。 不过，从她的说法来看，这个故事似乎还有更多的内情。 “你说得对。那个巨人并不知道，弥诺陶洛斯首领和他的新娘在他们与这个怪物的协议中加入了一种特殊的咒语——这种咒语需要他们的后代世世代代不断地投入自己的力量，才能在数个世纪之后完成它的形成。 但当这项工程完成后，那个巨兽就被束缚在了我们足部下的那座山下。如今，它留下的唯一痕迹，就是那些被科尔米诺斯用作光源的燃烧晶体。人们称它们为“山的血液”，因为据说这些晶体其实是那巨兽的血液渗出地面后形成的。 如今，再也没有鲜血被献给那些怪物了，它们的骨骼也被安放在神庙的骨灰室和地下墓穴中，以纪念死亡女神。不过，弥诺陶洛斯人依然会埋葬他们的死者，而我们提兰人很乐意帮助他们承担这一责任。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"Tira is most commonly known as the goddess of death and time — " she points to the hourglass clasp holding her black-and-gold garments together — "but she's also the patron of soldiers and kings, as well as that of nations and empires. Of all the Seven, she's got what's arguably the biggest and most diverse official portfolio. When you look at how people in different parts of the world revere the divines in their own way, there're often local idiosyncrasies to be had, such as how Keros is considered to have domain over agriculture in the far east, while sailors also tend to attribute not just storms, but governance of the sea itself to Sorra." [pc.bg acolyte |Yeah, not uncommon at all — it was a topic you'd come to be fairly familiar with in the course of your studies as an acolyte. Most people aren't aware of all the little details of local worship, although most do know that different peoples have their own interpretations of the gods' appearances |Now that's an interesting approach. You'd known that different peoples have had their own interpretations of the gods, but the differences were cosmetic and superficial at best ]. "Just because she's the goddess of death doesn't mean there's any need to fear her," Nihara continues. "She makes sure that the threads of our fates are cut at their appointed times — not before, and not after. Her followers are tasked with removing the lingering dead from this world and to end their suffering. She's reasonable, if you can convince her that it's necessary for her to stay her hand, if the need is great enough, she will; people have talked her into it before. There's a difference between a ceremonious ending... and otherwise." |Why is there a Tiran temple all the way out in the tunnels, anyway? As you understand it, there's a serviceable pantheon in Khor'minos proper where her colleagues took refuge in. "Well, the city is big, and space is at a premium — above, below and around. Given how many people there are in those walls, we wouldn't have the space to inter all of them. When you're a devotee of the goddess of death, you're made aware of just how many people pass in a day free of foul play, and conversely, how many people must be born in that same time. "That temple was originally founded with the help of the minotaur king of the time in order to use some of the old mining tunnels to lay the people of the city to their final rest, you understand. They were just there and empty, so he thought it'd be good to fill them up... these days, only the wealthy are capable of affording a spot in the city's catacombs proper, but some of the patricians opted to be buried near their country villas. That's... or rather, was, another of my jobs." You see. Nihara sighs. "My biggest concern, really, is that the goos that invaded the temple have tainted the corpses. Or even worse, the other way around. Normally, I'd be confident about the wards holding, but given the corruption's run so deep anything's possible at this point." |"I was never very much associated with the whole psychopomp aspect of the Tiran faith — as someone who was supposed to do outreach, the most I'd do was to prepare the initial rites if someone happened to pass away in the lakeshore district. Put them in gentle repose, then send for someone from the temple to take them away for the cremation, embalming, or however the family wanted the body disposed of before what was left got interred in the tunnels by the temple." The rites, huh... "People here aren't like Jassirans or Tronarrians, they're not that big into bringing their wealth with them into the next life and instead leaving their material things for their living issue to enjoy. What most of the Tiran rites about these parts did was to make sure the bones and other remains of people weren't stolen." Ugh.[pc.bg arcanist acolyte scholar | You have some idea of what they'd be wanted for. Nihara nods | Who would want to steal such things? Nihara sighs ]. "Those who would be looking for the remains of say, ancient minotaur kings or the great mothers to use in so-called enchanting, the same way you'd use a piece of a dragon to imbue an echo of its spirit into something valuable to you. As you can imagine, there've been several scandals of this sort before, which is why the minoan royalty personally took an interest in funding the temple out there in the tunnels. In wilder places like Valgarde, the people there take it a step further, considering it customary to cannibalize bites out of the glorious deceased in the hopes that they would get the traits of the dead. Tirans were instrumental in putting a stop to such barbaric practices that spread diseases, amongst other things. "But that's all beyond me. I'm just here to help people not fear the reaper so much, and make sure they're in tip-top shape for when she does call to them." |"We've never really had a big presence in this region — it used to be almost all Lumian primacy from the Greyvales up to the eastern coast, or at least that's what I was told. The pantheon in Khor'minos is mostly perfunctory when it comes to a bunch of the deities, with their statues being there just to be there. "But that's fine. Having fewer of us around just means that each one of us is more special, and we were never swamped or understaffed to begin with. Because I'm the only one to live out over the lake like this, it used to be that almost everyone in the patricians' villas and along the shore knew my face and called me by name. That felt really nice, I'll admit." |"Heheheh. You like my outfit, don't you? It's quite obvious, when I feel your eyes on me." Well, it is very eye-catching. If you didn't know better and it weren't for the obvious symbology, you'd have imagined it was some kind of exotic Mallachite get-up. Nihara tsks, wagging a finger in your direction. "Yes, yes, and I'm sure Lumians all uniformly wrap themselves from head to toe in body bags with only the eyes peeking out. Fact is that Mallach isn't the only one who understands the basics of good appeal, and since I was supposed to be face of the temple to the public as it were, I decided to play to my strengths. Being all shrouded and intimidating does have its own mystique, but it's not really the one you want to present when you're trying to convince others that your goddess is an approachable part of daily life." By showing off plenty of skin. "Hey, my skin needs to breathe, and I've got to be able to move freely while wearing all of this, swimming included. A girl like me's got needs, you know. But no. If it helps, I'm not the one who came up with this design — it's actually fairly commonplace back in Tronarii, I hear. Of course, since I've never been back there, I wouldn't be able to say for sure, but I don't see any reason to disbelieve it." |Did the local minotaurs always have the habit of interring their dead? Did it come with the Tiran faith here? The temple you passed by on the way to the city was old, but it still looked far newer than the adjoining tunnels. "Oh, no. While the burial tunnels adjoining the temple are old and the catacombs under Khor'minos even older, the practice of the minotaurs burying their dead like this predates their coming to believe in the seven divines. Although the Tirans did put a stop to many of the most cruel and barbaric practices, we accommodated as many of the more reasonable customs into the faith as possible, so long as they did not contravene the goddess' teachings." So it was an ancient minoan custom. Nihara taps her chin, looking thoughtful. "I believe so. Local legend has it that before the seven divines came to be known in this part of the world, a terrible giant of primordial earth and flame dwelled beneath this very mountain. It had developed quite a taste for the flesh of sapient beings, you see, and so flaming chasms were a common occurrence upon the mountains and the adjoining foothills and coast — opening in the blink of an eye to swallow the hapless and closing up again just as quickly." [flags.FIRE_TEMPLE |Come to think of it... you remember the temple of terrestrial fire back in the Frostwood. Was there any relation to this primordial being? Nihara shrugs. "I don't know what temple you speak of, but the peoples of this corner of the world used to worship many animistic spirits. It may be possible that the two are connected, it may be not, the minoan legends don't say. |That sounds pretty horrific, and yet it makes sense that the ancient minotaurs would revere such a being — out of fear, if nothing else. "Primordial beings and animistic spirits commanded a more... diverse approach to matters than the seven divines, [pc.name]. More unknowable and capricious, as befits a time of chaos lost to the earliest myths and legends. ] "Either way, a minotaur chieftain of the time discovered that his bride-to-be was slated to be the giant's next meal. The details are scant, but given the considerable motivation present he confronted the primordial being and managed to work out a deal: it would allow the people of the lands it dwelled under to live in relative peace, and in return every single being in the chieftain's domain, minotaur or otherwise, would be fed to the earth when they passed so the giant could feast upon all the flesh of the multitudes that could prosper upon a peaceful land. "The giant was a being of innate fire and endless hunger, but had enough greed in it to understand the concept of delayed gratification; there was sense in staying its hand for the moment so it could have more flesh later. The deal was struck, and the quakes, crevasses and lavaspouts stopped as long as the minotaurs interred the dead of all who dwelled in their expanding kingdom." The way she tells it, there's more to the story, though. "You're right. Unbeknownst to the giant, the minotaur chief and his bride fashioned a charm into their agreement with the monster, a charm that would take centuries beyond their deaths to complete as each generation of their kin so consumed fed fragments of their own power into it. But when it was completed, the giant was bound beneath the mountain far below our feet, the only trace of it today being the burning crystals that Khor'minos uses as lights. Blood of the mountain, they call it, as it's supposedly droplets of the giant's blood as it seeps to the surface. "Now, no more flesh is fed to the monster, and bones lie in quiet repose within the temple ossuary and catacombs in honor of the goddess of death. But the minotaurs continue to bury their dead anyway, and we Tirans are happy to ease them through that burden." ] "

rows.original: [rand |"Do you know it sometimes rains down here, over the lake?" Does it? Rain's usually the last thing on one's mind when one's miles under the earth in the heart of a mountain. Nihara laughs at that. "Well, it's not exactly rain — I've only seen that a few times when I've had to leave the undermountain on business. The clouds, the wind... and of course, the rain. But we also get water falling from above on occasion, believe it or not. I don't know how it works, but the air about the river and lake's pretty humid and it all gathers up above. I don't know if there's a cistern or pool or something in the twinkling darkness up there, but every so often something gives and it just starts pouring down all over the lake and the shore. Do that enough times over the years, and it's how you get a lake like this." Yeah. You agree with Nihara that you're not sure you'd call it rain, but it's as close a facsimile of it as might be reasonable to get this far underground. "I wouldn't call it less than actual rain, just different. Each one's got their own charms to it — there's this earthy smell you get when it pours down here, like hard water with a bit of mushroom mixed in, and it's just as good as the smells you get before and after rain when you're on the surface. But I guess that's another reason why I love living here so much." |"It used to be great here. You can see the lakeshore from here and think it's a desolate place, but the sandy beach used to have all sorts of people on a good day. Wasn't just the locals from their villas and those those who served them, but also people who'd come down from the city to see the lights out over the lake. Their voices would come out to me over the water — far enough to maintain a comfortable distance, yet close enough to bring some form of life in through my windows. "Now that they're gone, I kind of miss them. You don't realize how something so seemingly small can be so important until it's gone. Even the people selling warm treats from their carts... ah. The place doesn't feel calm to me, it feels dead, mostly because there're still so many remnants of those who used to come here." ... Nihara shakes her head. "Sorry about that, I let my melancholy get away with me when you're the one who needs comforting, not me; you're the one who goes out into the tunnels and beyond, after all. Why don't you let me make it up to you?" |"All the damp makes it easy for mushrooms and other fungi to grow — a lot of them even incorporate water into their being somehow. I've even got a clump of lunar buckets right out in the garden that don't just light up the place, but also draw water from the lake and filter it for use." Yeah. Even from here, the glow from the lake's western shore is visible, kind of like the sunset on the horizon, only blue. And the way it glints off the water... "Really pretty, isn't it? It's like how I remember moonlight on water, only blue." Hmm, you're not sure of the comparison yourself, but it has its own allure in the same way that the "stars" in the cavern ceiling aren't really stars, but do their own unique thing and that's just as good in their own way. "A-anyways. There aren't any trees down here, so most people use the thicker mushroom stalks as a substitute when you dry them. They're also pretty resistant to both dryness and damp, so there's that... the better quality of the material didn't stop the wealthy from importing timber all the way from outside just to show off that they could, though. I feel kinda bad seeing such things, knowing it's a terrible waste, but the patricians have always been about flaunting their wealth in the most ostentatious manner as far back as anyone can remember." |"The lake has very good water. While I wouldn't recommend doing it all the time, you could just scoop up a handful and simply drink straight from it, if that's what you wanted." You suspect that such cleanliness didn't come to be of its own accord. "Oh yes. While there's no one around to enforce it at the moment, anyone who was caught throwing trash into the lake got dragged all the way into the colosseum plaza and was flogged there in full view of the public. Didn't matter if you were a citizen, either — you got flogged anyway. The patricians have sunk a lot into their countryside villas, and they don't take kindly to people fouling up their nice neighborhood. "Then there's the matter of the lakebed — you know that pool in so many minoan houses that purifies water? They got the idea from the lakebed here, with all the sand and gravel that the water trickles through. Add to that all the mushrooms that grow out from the water and filter the nutrients they need from the lake itself, like those I've planted in my garden, and you see why it's so pure. Little in the way of trash goes in, and there're so many things removing filth from it at the same time. It takes so much effort to keep things nice for other people — if there's one thing I've learned by living with the minotaurs for so long, it's that civilization doesn't come about by accident." |So, this is the rich district away from the rich district, then. Nihara nods. "Just like you and me, the minotaur patricians need to get away from it all. Unlike you and me, they actually have the means to do so. The bright lights of the city wear off after a while, and one wishes to have the peace of one's country holdings. Over time, people came from the city proper in order to fill the demands of the patricians in their respite... and so here we are. "The sand, the water, the so-called stars in the cavern ceiling... oh, yes. Nature's close enough to be appreciated, but not so close that it gets up in your everything. I will say that the minotaurs do know how to make things look regal and beautiful all at once. A countryside paradise, as it goes in the undermountain — up until all this happened. I'm very blessed to have lived here, and still be able to do so even if it's a little tougher now. These are comforts that people the world over will never know, and I've got to remember to be grateful for that." ]
rows.translation: [rand |你知道吗，有时候这里也会下雨，就在湖面上。” “真的吗？当人们身处山腹深处、几英里深的地底下时，雨水通常根本不是会想到的事情。” 尼原听到这里笑了起来。 嗯，其实那并不完全算是雨——我只见过几次这种情况，每次都是因为工作需要离开地下山城。那些云层、风……当然，还有雨。不过，你可能很难相信，有时候也会有一些水从天上掉下来。 我不知道这是怎么形成的，但河流和湖泊周围的空气湿度很高，这些湿气会聚集在上方。我不知道在那些闪烁的黑暗中是否有什么蓄水池或水坑之类的东西，但每隔一段时间，就会有一些东西破裂，然后雨水就会倾泻下来，覆盖整个湖泊和湖岸。 多年来，如果反复这样做，最终就会形成这样的湖泊。” “是啊。你和尼原一样，也不确定自己是否会用这样的说法来描述它。 雨虽然这已经是在地下这么深的地方所能做到的最接近原貌的仿制了，但我不会称之为…… 较少 比起真正的雨水，这些雨也有它们独特的魅力。每场雨都有自己独特的气息——当雨水倾泻而下时，会有一种泥土的气息，就像是含有少量蘑菇香味的硬水一样。这种味道，与你在雨前雨后站在地面上时所感受到的那些气味一样美妙。我想，这也是我如此热爱居住在这里的原因之一吧。 rows.raw: " [rand |"Do you know it sometimes rains down here, over the lake?" Does it? Rain's usually the last thing on one's mind when one's miles under the earth in the heart of a mountain. Nihara laughs at that. "Well, it's not exactly rain — I've only seen that a few times when I've had to leave the undermountain on business. The clouds, the wind... and of course, the rain. But we also get water falling from above on occasion, believe it or not. I don't know how it works, but the air about the river and lake's pretty humid and it all gathers up above. I don't know if there's a cistern or pool or something in the twinkling darkness up there, but every so often something gives and it just starts pouring down all over the lake and the shore. Do that enough times over the years, and it's how you get a lake like this." Yeah. You agree with Nihara that you're not sure you'd call it rain, but it's as close a facsimile of it as might be reasonable to get this far underground. "I wouldn't call it less than actual rain, just different. Each one's got their own charms to it — there's this earthy smell you get when it pours down here, like hard water with a bit of mushroom mixed in, and it's just as good as the smells you get before and after rain when you're on the surface. But I guess that's another reason why I love living here so much." |"It used to be great here. You can see the lakeshore from here and think it's a desolate place, but the sandy beach used to have all sorts of people on a good day. Wasn't just the locals from their villas and those those who served them, but also people who'd come down from the city to see the lights out over the lake. Their voices would come out to me over the water — far enough to maintain a comfortable distance, yet close enough to bring some form of life in through my windows. "Now that they're gone, I kind of miss them. You don't realize how something so seemingly small can be so important until it's gone. Even the people selling warm treats from their carts... ah. The place doesn't feel calm to me, it feels dead, mostly because there're still so many remnants of those who used to come here." ... Nihara shakes her head. "Sorry about that, I let my melancholy get away with me when you're the one who needs comforting, not me; you're the one who goes out into the tunnels and beyond, after all. Why don't you let me make it up to you?" |"All the damp makes it easy for mushrooms and other fungi to grow — a lot of them even incorporate water into their being somehow. I've even got a clump of lunar buckets right out in the garden that don't just light up the place, but also draw water from the lake and filter it for use." Yeah. Even from here, the glow from the lake's western shore is visible, kind of like the sunset on the horizon, only blue. And the way it glints off the water... "Really pretty, isn't it? It's like how I remember moonlight on water, only blue." Hmm, you're not sure of the comparison yourself, but it has its own allure in the same way that the "stars" in the cavern ceiling aren't really stars, but do their own unique thing and that's just as good in their own way. "A-anyways. There aren't any trees down here, so most people use the thicker mushroom stalks as a substitute when you dry them. They're also pretty resistant to both dryness and damp, so there's that... the better quality of the material didn't stop the wealthy from importing timber all the way from outside just to show off that they could, though. I feel kinda bad seeing such things, knowing it's a terrible waste, but the patricians have always been about flaunting their wealth in the most ostentatious manner as far back as anyone can remember." |"The lake has very good water. While I wouldn't recommend doing it all the time, you could just scoop up a handful and simply drink straight from it, if that's what you wanted." You suspect that such cleanliness didn't come to be of its own accord. "Oh yes. While there's no one around to enforce it at the moment, anyone who was caught throwing trash into the lake got dragged all the way into the colosseum plaza and was flogged there in full view of the public. Didn't matter if you were a citizen, either — you got flogged anyway. The patricians have sunk a lot into their countryside villas, and they don't take kindly to people fouling up their nice neighborhood. "Then there's the matter of the lakebed — you know that pool in so many minoan houses that purifies water? They got the idea from the lakebed here, with all the sand and gravel that the water trickles through. Add to that all the mushrooms that grow out from the water and filter the nutrients they need from the lake itself, like those I've planted in my garden, and you see why it's so pure. Little in the way of trash goes in, and there're so many things removing filth from it at the same time. It takes so much effort to keep things nice for other people — if there's one thing I've learned by living with the minotaurs for so long, it's that civilization doesn't come about by accident." |So, this is the rich district away from the rich district, then. Nihara nods. "Just like you and me, the minotaur patricians need to get away from it all. Unlike you and me, they actually have the means to do so. The bright lights of the city wear off after a while, and one wishes to have the peace of one's country holdings. Over time, people came from the city proper in order to fill the demands of the patricians in their respite... and so here we are. "The sand, the water, the so-called stars in the cavern ceiling... oh, yes. Nature's close enough to be appreciated, but not so close that it gets up in your everything. I will say that the minotaurs do know how to make things look regal and beautiful all at once. A countryside paradise, as it goes in the undermountain — up until all this happened. I'm very blessed to have lived here, and still be able to do so even if it's a little tougher now. These are comforts that people the world over will never know, and I've got to remember to be grateful for that." ] "

"H-hmph. If that is what you're going to demand of me, you ask the question first." ] |[rand |"Ooof. I'm fine. Tired, but fine. Thanks for asking, [pc.name], it does feel like I've got an ocean inside of me at times." Heaving a happy sigh, Nihara wriggles about in her chair, curling her tails about her big pregnant belly, and you see all of her slosh. Not just her full tits and tummy, but also her hips and thighs... her body must be collecting a lot of fluid in order to feed the little gookitten when it's ready to be born. "Oh, that's an understatement. My body feels so heavy, but at the same time it feels so good; if I didn't have anything else to do I'd be curled up all day sleeping. And don't you make any jokes about feline lethargy, please." What? You? Of course you wouldn't make any cruel jokes at a poor goocat's expense, would you? Smiling, Nihara sets both hands on her protruding, round belly and rubs away lovingly. "After all that's happened, it's good to be able to feel happy and hopeful once more, even if it's not quite over yet. When I go out on my rounds and see all the people holed up in their villas lose their fear if even for a little while just to pet the little kitten inside of me... it really makes my heart sing. "Fear and despair are surer killers than blades in this kind of situation, [pc.name]. While I can't wholly approve of the minotaur king running the circuses at full tilt even when there are demons at the walls, it is important to keep the morale of the people up, even if it's by such... wasteful means. It's not right to... delude the people of what they might be facing should it come to that, but at the same time I don't see any way they could be hardened to the situation, and the circuses are just making the problem worse. At least out here no one has any illusions as to what's at stake, and it takes a certain kind of mindset to stubbornly remain on one's property rather than flee for the safety of the city." |"Sometimes, I'll just feel really thirsty for no reason at all, my mouth and tongue drying out and becoming all kinds of awkward. Then I go ahead and drink a whole jug or two until I feel my stomach sloshing along with my womb... not that it slakes my thirst any, of course, but at least I can't drink any more. Then the sensation passes, as abruptly as it came..." It has to be tiring for her. Nihara gives you a thin smile. "It's not bad or anything, and all the good I've gotten out of being with child far outweighs this simple annoyance, so I've neither qualms nor regrets about it. But you did ask, so I told you. It's important to be honest with people you know, and in return be able to trust them. I've already got your kittens growing inside of me, what need is there for any remaining barriers between us?" |"Aah, it won't be long before the kitten's going to be born." Purring contentedly, Nihara cradles her big swollen belly in her hands, one hand atop it and the other under. "A little water wyrd." Looking at the size of her kitten bump, there's little doubt about that — if Nihara gets any bigger, she might just explode like an overfilled waterskin. And speaking of overfilled waterskins... the comparison really isn't off. The full, solid weight causes even her firm womb to hang below her waist, heaving in and out as if filled with intensely dense fluid that weighs far more than simple volume would suggest. "Sush, shush. Your seed's almost done growing inside of me. Just a little more... so do have patience. If you want to touch it, [pc.name], all you have to do is ask." That's a tempting offer... maybe you'll take her up on it, so long as she can contain herself while you're doing it. Nihara's purring drops one or two octaves, and her ears turn forward as her smile widens. "Sorry about that, [pc.name] — could you please repeat what you just said there? I'm not quite sure I heard you correctly." ] ] ] "

rows.original: [nihara.isCorrupted |[rand |"Oh, the kittens? I let them loose in the lake during the day, and they mostly mind themselves." That's... a little troubling. But you shouldn't make assumptions about how well young water wyrds are able to care for themselves. Nihara leans in and gives you a light kiss. "Don't worry about it in the least. The lake is completely safe, I know everything that goes on in it, and their young minds are stimulated by the wonders of nature. Think of the waters as a very large playpen — they won't be bothered by anyone or anything so long as they stay in the lake, and they instinctively do just that. And what is a water wyrd going to do? Drown?" She's still very cavalier about it all and you can't shake of the sense of unease over infants being given free range of the lake, even if it's their home, but presumably she knows best how to raise her kind. "Oh, don't get the wrong idea. Those kittens are all over me once they get hungry or if they want my attention, but other than that they're all too content to be left to their own devices. It's not as if I'm not the kind to be a bad mother, not with such loving personality, am I? It's just how we are, and how we're brought up." |"Mmm... I love each and every one of the gookittens we made together, [pc.name]," Nihara purrs, her tails swaying in your direction. "Hearing their soft mewls when I hug them, or feeling them paw at my chest when they want to be nursed... so demanding, but I know they get that from you." Oh? And she thinks she's not demanding as well? But seriously, you're just glad that she's not regretting her decision in the least. "Hmm, I can't say I wasn't worried at first, allowing you to convince me to take the leap, [pc.name]. But at this point, there's no way I could ever imagine going back on all of this. Not when I cuddle up with my kittens when I go to rest, with little bodies pressed up against me... "[nihara.isPregnant |Actually, with the way I'm feeling right now, I wouldn't mind being up for some more once I'm done with these buns in my oven..." She isn't even done with being pregnant, and she's already thinking of more? Gods, maybe she should pace herself. "Oh, I might change my mind, my dear [pc.name], but I wouldn't bet on it. I am a woman who knows exactly what she wants, after all. |In fact, [pc.name], I do love them all so much that if you're up for it, I wouldn't mind making one or two more... are you up to the task, my dear? ]" |Purring, Nihara leans in close and cups her hefty tits, pushing them up and together so that they leak just a little. "It's amazing how much kittens have to drink, isn't it? It's not as if it's something I didn't know to begin with, but experiencing it for oneself really puts some perspective on the matter. They're growing kittens, and they need a lot to stay hydrated, being mostly water... which means I need to stay hydrated plenty as well. It's quite vexing, I'd say." Well, she does live above an entire lake, so there shouldn't be any trouble getting water. Nihara doesn't say anything to that, instead simply leaning forward in her chair and holding your gaze with that same little disquieting smile. It's painfully clear after a few moments of this that when she said hydration, she didn't mean water... |"You know, [pc.name], I didn't realize that I desired it before, but now that I've had kittens of my own, I'm determined to want a big family." Curious. What sparked this realization? It's not as if it's anything new; the local minotaurs certainly aren't shy about their desires in that regard. "I... I can't really put it into words, but I know full well what I want, [pc.name], I want it really badly, and I'm not about to be ashamed of saying so. Maybe you might call it an addiction to giving birth... I prefer to know it as the surety that there's something mysterious about having life growing inside of you that fills one's heart... and the firm weight of a kitten or two. "I'm sure that having helped set me on this path, you wouldn't mind helping me see it to its end, would you?" ...Ye gods, what might you just have unleashed here? "That's an attitude I'd love to see more of, [pc.name]," Nihara purrs, patting [nihara.pregStage 1 2 3 |the bulgy swell of her tummy |the firm, protruding swell of her kitten bump |the obscenely huge dome of her overstuffed womb |her flat tummy ]. "I'll be counting on you to do your part, okay?" |"Mmm... I don't know why, but I find myself craving more kittens..." [nihara.isPregnant |You know that Nihara's already in a motherly way, so for her to have such desires well ahead of time is... well, getting ahead of herself, to say the least. Unless she's saying that she can conceive more kittens while already pregnant... now wouldn't that be a sight to see, even if quite shocking. |Your eyes wander down to Nihara's lightly-muscled midriff, and your goocat lover teasingly flexes her abs, knowing full well that you're watching. Oh, she's healthy and more than willing to go... ] Is there... any particular reason, though? "Do I need a reason beyond simply liking it?" A small, disquieting smile on her lips, Nihara [nihara.isPregnant |shamelessly rubs her hands all over her rounded belly, blatantly taking pleasure in the act |leans in and blows you a kiss. ] "You know, [pc.name], when I was younger I'd hear of cowgirls who just wound up having massive families. They got started with one, and quickly found themselves just happening to have another, and another, and another... poor things just couldn't explain why although they knew they should really pace themselves, the calves just kept coming. Poor things couldn't help it — they just kept on slipping and falling, right onto the nearest, thickest prick, and wound up getting pregnant over and over again. "You could say they just about got addicted to it..." Um... Nihara purrs. "Oh, look at the expression on your face right now. I was mostly teasing, mostly. After all, if I'd really sunk to those depths I'd have jumped your bones already and mated with you as many times as it'd take to drain you completely dry, but I'm still here, aren't I? That being said, it's not out of the question that a poor helpless water wyrd like me could end up getting addicted to this if left unhydrated for too long..." ] |[rand |"Some might call having kittens in a time like this irresponsible, but after I let myself be convinced by you to make the leap, I haven't regretted it in the least. The moment I held the little mewling gooball in my arms, I knew I would move the world for my kittens." That's a very positive outlook on life, and it suits someone as peppy as her. "Sure, the tunnels may be running over with imps, but that's just an impetus to make my home safer than it already is. Water wyrds before me have raised kittens in war and peace, in lean times and plenty. It wasn't always perfect, but if my ancestors managed to keep on doing what they were doing during the Godswar, then I really don't have any excuse to give into fear of the future. After all, Tira teaches us to fear neither time nor death; her embrace is warm, and we are promised the length of our lives before fate cuts them short. "It's hope for the future, don't you know? And that's what's important — it's another reason to keep on going in a situation like this when there's no end in sight." Well, if she wants to make some more little gookittens... all she needs to do is ask. "Tsk. So forward." |Looking around Nihara's home does bring up one thing: while you know she's had your gookittens, you don't see anything resembling a nursery anywhere in her home. Not a crib to be seen, to be honest... "A crib? Gods forbid," Nihara replies, raising a hand to her mouth and giggling. "Not only would everything get damp, but your kittens would just ooze out from between the sides and land on the ground. Then I'd have a crying kitten with a nasty bump, and no one wants that." You understood that last part, but... ooze out from between the sides? "Water wyrds are a lot more pliant when we're young. My dad said it has something to do with us not having as strongly developed a sense of self or something, but apparently I couldn't be contained when I was a kitten, not that I remembered any of it to begin with. Anyway, a crib makes no sense. When I go to bed, I have the kittens cuddle up to me like a real mom cat would." And where do they go during the day? Who's taking care of them while she's out and about making her rounds or picking over the abandoned villas? "Oh, they just go into one of the bathing pools. Baby water wyrds dry out a lot easier then grown-ups or even children, so it's important to keep the young ones moist. While I know they'll be able to subsist on clean water for a bit before I can get home to nurse them, I can't help but feel a little guilty every time I've to lock up the house." It is what it is — she has to do what she has to in order to be a decent mother. All this talk about gookittens and all the special things they need to grow up well just makes your head spin, you're not sure you'd be able to get it all no matter how much Nihara explains it. |"Sometimes I wake up in the night, and my first thought is immediate terror that I might've rolled over and squashed one of my kittens. Then I realize that even if I'd done that, they'd just have flowed away to begin with. I don't know why, but in that single moment of utter fear and followed by gasping relief before cuddling the kittens close and heading back to sleep... I feel like I've experienced the totality of what it means to be a mother. That's almost certainly not the case, of course, and yet the feelings are so strong that they leave me shaking, whether it be with fear or joy." ... "Hold me?" For the woman who had your kittens? Gladly. Nihara gratefully sinks into the hug, and you can tell that being a mother's changed her in both the physical and mental senses. You hold for a moment, savoring the cool touch of skin and water-goo alike, and then finally pull away, leaving Nihara a little woozy. "Oh dear. I haven't felt so intense for a while now. But then again, everything around you seems to wind up that way eventually." She's a mother now, and that opens one's eyes to the world to see it in a new light, or so you've been told. It's just a small shift in perspective, but an important one nevertheless. |Sighing in satisfaction, Nihara leans in close and cups her hefty tits, pushing them up and together so that they leak just a little. "It's amazing how much kittens have to drink, isn't it? It's not as if it's something I didn't know to begin with, but experiencing it for oneself really puts some perspective on the matter. They're growing kittens, and they need a lot to stay hydrated, being mostly water... which means I need to stay hydrated plenty as well. It's quite vexing, I'd say; there's that need in the back of my mind all the time, an itch that demands to be scratched." Well, she does live above an entire lake, so there shouldn't be any trouble getting water. Nihara doesn't say anything to that, instead simply leaning forward in her chair and holding your gaze with a little awkward smile. It's painfully clear after a few moments of this that when she said hydration, she didn't mean water... |"Your kittens are so full of energy, especially when they're in the water. I can tell that they have a bit of wanderlust in them, just like you — they're always champing at the bit to be let out into the wider areas of the lake and explore as they please." Is that safe for them, though? While they may be in their element as water wyrds, you have to remember that the gookittens are little more than newborns. The fact that they can swim like fish doesn't mean much when that's to be expected of kittens their age. "With the relic protecting the lake, they'll be fine so long as I'm there to watch over them. And of course, I'm always there every time I let them out. It's tempting to be overprotective, but you've got to give even the very young a controlled environment to play in, and I don't see anywhere else in this entire mountain that could be safer for them than this very lake." Ah, of course. "Really... the kittens have nothing but extremes. Either they're bursting with energy and scampering and swimming all over the place, or draped limply over the nearest open surface. I haven't been a mother that long, and I'm already getting used to carrying kittens back to the lake house with me. At least I still remember how my own mother used to carry me around by the scruff of my neck when I was really little... that quiets them down really quickly." ] ]
rows.translation: [nihara.isCorrupted |[rand |哦，那些小猫吗？我白天把它们放到了湖里，它们大多时候都能自己照顾好自己。” 不过……这有点让人担心。不过，我们也不应该想当然地认为这些年幼的水域生物真的有能力照顾好自己。 尼原凑过来，轻轻地吻了你一下。“完全不必担心。那个湖非常安全，我知道湖里发生的一切，而且孩子们的大脑会因为大自然的奇妙而变得活跃起来。可以把那些水想象成一个巨大的游乐场——只要他们待在湖里，就不会受到任何人和事物的干扰，而他们也会本能地选择待在湖里。 那么，水之精灵会怎么做呢？难道会淹死它们吗？ 她对此仍然显得非常漫不经心，而当你看到那些幼崽在湖里自由活动时，还是会不由得感到不安——尽管这里本来就是它们的家园。不过，想必她最清楚该如何抚养自己的同类吧。 哦，别误会。那些小猫一旦饿了，或者想要引起我的注意，就会缠着我不放，但除此之外，它们其实都很满足，愿意自己待着。我并不是那种不称职的妈妈，毕竟我这么有爱心，对吧？ 这就是我们的天性，也是我们成长过程中所形成的习惯。 |嗯……我真的很喜欢我们一起制作的每一只小猫玩具…… [pc.name]喵，”尼哈拉轻声说道，它的尾巴摇摆着朝你的方向摆动。“当我抱住它们时，听到它们轻轻的喵喵声；当它们想要被喂奶时，感受到它们用爪子轻触我的胸口……它们真是太贪心了，不过我知道，这些它们都是从你这里得到的。” 哦？它还觉得自己并不贪心呢？不过说真的，你只是庆幸它丝毫没有后悔自己的决定罢了。 “嗯，刚开始我确实很担心，不过还是在你说服下，我决定尝试这个决定。 [pc.name]但是，在这个时候，我根本无法想象自己会放弃这一切。尤其是当我休息的时候，那些小猫会依偎在我身边，它们的小身体紧紧贴着我……[nihara.isPregnant |其实，以我现在的状态来说，等这些面包烤好后，我倒也不介意再要几个…… 她甚至还没结束怀孕期，就已经在考虑要再要孩子了？天哪，也许她应该适当控制一下自己的节奏。 “哦，亲爱的，我也许会改变主意的。 [pc.name]不过，我不敢肯定。我…… 是 毕竟，她是一个非常清楚自己想要什么的女人。 |事实上， [pc.name]我真的很喜欢它们，所以如果你愿意的话，我并不介意再制作一两个……亲爱的，你有没有能力完成这个任务呢？ ]" |喵喵叫着，尼哈拉凑近了一些，将她那丰满的胸部托起来，把它们挤压在一起，让乳汁稍微渗出一些。“小猫们需要喝这么多水，真是不可思议吧？其实我本来就知道这个道理，但亲身体会之后，才真正明白了其中的意义。它们正在成长，需要大量的水分来保持身体机能的正常运转，而它们的身体成分大部分都是水……也就是说…… 我 也需要多喝水来保持身体水分平衡。说实话，这真的挺让人烦恼的。” “嗯，她住在一片湖泊的上方，所以获取水源应该不会有什么问题。” 尼哈拉对此没有发表任何评论，只是微微前倾身体，用那种令人不安的微笑注视着对方。几秒钟后，就再明显不过了——当她提到“保持水分平衡”时，她指的并不是水…… |你知道， [pc.name]之前我并没有意识到自己有这样的愿望，但现在自己有了小猫，我就下定决心要有一个大家庭。” 真奇怪，是什么引发了这种想法呢？其实这并不是什么新鲜的事情；当地的弥诺陶洛斯在这方面也从不掩饰自己的愿望。 “我……实在很难用语言表达出来，但我心里很清楚自己想要什么。 想要, [pc.name]我真的很渴望得到它，而且我毫不羞于承认这一点。也许你可以将这种渴望称为一种对“生育”的依赖……但我更愿意将其视为一种确信：当生命在你体内孕育、逐渐成长时，那种感觉确实会充满人的内心。还有那一两只小猫带来的沉甸甸的重量…… “我相信，既然你曾经帮助我走上了这条道路，你一定不介意继续帮助我走完这条路吧？” …… 天啊，你究竟在这里引发了什么事情呢？ 这种态度我真的很希望看到更多人能够具备。 [pc.name]喵，”尼原一边轻声说道，一边轻轻拍着…… [nihara.pregStage 1 2 3 |她凸出的腹部 |她的小猫肚子上那块凸出的肉包 |她那庞大得离谱的、充满胎块的子宫 |平坦的小腹 ]我就指望你能够尽到自己的责任，好吗？ |嗯……我不知道为什么，但我突然觉得特别想再养几只小猫…… [nihara.isPregnant |你知道，尼原她本来就有一种母性本能，所以她这么早就产生这样的想法……嗯，至少可以说，她有点太急功近利了。除非她是想说，在已经怀孕的情况下还能再生小猫……那样的话，虽然听起来可能有点不可思议，但确实会是一件非常有趣的事情。 |你的目光不由自主地落在了尼哈拉那结实的小腹上，而这个喜欢调戏你的女孩也故意地绷紧了腹部肌肉，她完全知道你在看。哦，她真的很健康，而且也非常乐意这样做…… ] 不过，有没有什么特别的理由呢？ “除了单纯地喜欢它之外，我还需要别的理由吗？”尼哈拉嘴角浮现出一丝令人不安的微笑。 [nihara.isPregnant |她毫无羞耻地把手放在自己圆润的腹部上，明显地从这一举动中获得乐趣。 |凑近过来，给你一个吻。 ] 你知道， [pc.name]在我年轻的时候，我常常听说那些女牛仔最终都会生下很多孩子。她们一开始只有一个孩子，但很快就会发现自己又有了第二个、第三个……这些可怜的女人们根本不明白为什么会发生这样的事，虽然她们知道应该控制生育节奏，但孩子就是一个接一个地来到世上。 这些可怜的生物实在无能为力——它们不断地滑倒、跌落，总是正好落在那些最粗壮、最尖锐的物体上，结果一次又一次地怀孕了。 “可以说，它们简直对此上瘾了。嗯……” 尼哈拉轻轻哼了一声，说道：“哦，看看你现在脸上的表情。我刚才主要是在开玩笑而已。 主要是毕竟，如果我真的堕落到那种地步，早就对你下手部了，会和你交配无数次，直到把你彻底耗尽为止。但我现在还在这里，不是吗？话虽如此，对于像我这样可怜又无助的水之精灵来说，如果继续这样下去，也完全有可能会上瘾的。 未补充水分的 太久了…… ] |[rand |在这样的时刻生小猫，有些人可能会认为这是不负责任的行为，但在你说服我做出这个决定之后，我丝毫没有后悔。当我把那个发出呜呜声的小家伙抱在怀里的那一刻，我就知道，我会为我的小猫们付出一切。这种对生活的积极态度真的很适合她这样充满活力的人。” “当然了，虽然隧道里可能到处都是小妖精，但这也正好能激励我把家弄得比现在更加安全。 在我之前，水之族的人们无论在战争还是和平时期，无论在艰难还是富足的时刻，都一直抚养着小猫。这样的生活并不总是完美的，但如果我的祖先们在“神战”期间能够坚持他们所做的事情，那么我真的没有任何理由去害怕未来。 毕竟，蒂拉教会我们不要畏惧时间，也不要畏惧死亡；她的怀抱充满温暖，她还承诺我们会活到命运提前终结我们的那一天。 “这就是对未来的希望，你难道不明白吗？而这正是最重要的——在这样的处境中，当似乎没有尽头的时候，这就是继续前行的另一个理由。嗯，如果她还想再养一些小家伙的话……她只需要开口请求就行了。 “啧，那就继续吧。 |环顾尼哈拉的家，确实会发现一件奇怪的事：虽然你知道她养过你的小猫，但在她的家里却根本看不到任何类似婴儿房的痕迹。说实话，连一张婴儿床都没有…… “婴儿床？天哪，那可不行，”尼哈拉一边说，一边用手捂住嘴，咯咯地笑了起来，“不仅所有东西都会弄湿，而且你的小猫肯定会从床边爬出来掉到地上。那样的话，我就会有只撞到头、哭个不停的小猫了，谁也不想遇到这种事情吧。 你明白最后那部分的意思，但是……那些水是从两侧渗出来的吗？ “当我们还小的时候，水精灵会变得更加柔软。我爸爸说，这可能与我们还没有形成很强的自我意识有关，但显然，在我还是小猫的时候，我根本无法被限制在某个范围内活动，不过我其实并不记得那些事情了。总之，用婴儿床来限制我根本是没有意义的。每当我睡觉的时候，那些小猫就会像真正的母猫一样依偎在我身边。 那么，它们在白天会去哪里呢？当她外出巡视或检查那些被废弃的别墅时，谁会照顾它们呢？ “哦，它们会进入其中一个游泳池里。幼小的生物比成年人或孩子更容易缺水，所以保持它们的身体湿润非常重要。虽然我知道在我回家喂它们之前，它们可以暂时靠干净的水生存，但每次我不得不锁上门离开时，还是会感到有些内疚。 事实就是如此——她必须做那些该做的事情，才能成为一个称职的母亲。那些关于小猫宝宝以及它们成长所需的各种特殊条件的讨论，真的会让人感到头晕目眩，无论尼哈拉怎么解释，你也不确定自己是否能够做到这一切。 |有时候我在夜里醒来，第一个念头就是会立刻感到恐惧——担心自己可能会翻身压到其中一只小猫。但随后我就会想到，即使真的发生了这种事，那些小猫本来也可能会自己滑开来的。 我不知道为什么，但在那一刻，当我感到极度恐惧，随后又因为松了一口气而紧紧抱住那些小猫，然后再次入睡……我觉得自己真正体会到了作为母亲的全部意义。 当然，情况几乎肯定不是这样的，但这种感受实在太强烈了，以至于让我不由得发抖——无论是出于恐惧还是喜悦。 那个曾经照顾过你家小猫的女人吗？当然愿意。 尼哈拉满怀感激地投入了你的怀抱，你可以明显感觉到，成为母亲这一经历在她的身体和心理上都产生了变化。你们拥抱了一会儿，你尽情享受着她那既柔软又带着水珠的肌肤带来的触感，最后才慢慢分开，让尼哈拉感到有些头晕目眩。 哦，天哪。我已经有一段时间没有感受到这样的强烈情绪了。不过，话说回来，你周围的一切似乎最终都会变成那样的。” 她现在已经成为一位母亲了，而这种经历似乎会让人们以一种全新的视角来看待这个世界，至少是人们常说的那样。 这只是一个视角上的微小变化，但无论如何，这个变化都是非常重要的。 |尼原满意地叹了口气，凑近身体，将自己那丰满的胸部托起来，让它们稍微聚拢一些，于是乳汁便有一点点渗了出来。“小猫们需要喝这么多水，真是不可思议吧？其实我本来就明白这个道理，但亲身体会之后，才真正明白了其中的意义。它们正在成长，需要大量的水分来保持身体机能的正常运转——毕竟它们的身体大部分都是由水构成的……所以说啊…… 我 同样，也需要保证充足的水分摄入。说实话，这真的挺让人烦恼的——这种需求一直萦绕在我的脑海中，就像一种必须得到满足的渴望。 不过，她住在一片湖泊的上方，所以获取水源应该不会有任何问题。 尼原对此没有说什么，只是微微前倾身体，坐在椅子上，用略带尴尬的笑容注视着你。过了片刻后，人们便清楚地意识到：当她提到“补水”时，她指的并不是水。.. |你的小猫们充满活力，尤其是在水里的时候。我能看出它们身上有一股探索的欲望，就像你一样——它们总是迫不及待地想要被放出去，去湖的更广阔的区域里自由探索。 不过，这对它们来说真的安全吗？虽然作为水生生物，它们可能非常适应水中的生活，但你们必须记住，这些小家伙其实还只是刚出生的幼崽。尽管它们能够像鱼一样游泳，但这对于它们这个年龄段的幼崽来说，其实也是理所当然的。 有这件护湖神器在，只要我在旁边守护着他们，他们就不会有危险。当然，每次我把他们放出去的时候，我都会在附近守着。虽然过度保护有点过分，但即便是年幼的孩子们，也需要一个有安全保障的环境来玩耍。在这整座山上，我觉得没有哪个地方比这个湖泊更安全了。 啊，当然。 “真的……这些小猫的行为总是走极端。要么精力充沛地在到处跑来跑去、游泳嬉戏，要么就无精打采地趴在最近的平面上。我当妈妈才没多久，就已经习惯了把小猫们带回湖边的小屋。至少我还记得，我小时候，妈妈总是抓着我的脖子把我抱在怀里……这样就能很快让它们安静下来。 ] ]
rows.raw: " [nihara.isCorrupted |[rand |"Oh, the kittens? I let them loose in the lake during the day, and they mostly mind themselves." That's... a little troubling. The lake is completely safe, I know everything that goes on in it, and their young minds are stimulated by the wonders of nature. Think of the waters as a very large playpen — they won't be bothered by anyone or anything so long as they stay in the lake, and they instinctively do just that. And what is a water wyrd going to do? Drown?" She's still very cavalier about it all and you can't shake of the sense of unease over infants being given free range of the lake, even if it's their home, but presumably she knows best how to raise her kind. "Oh, don't get the wrong idea. Those kittens are all over me once they get hungry or if they want my attention, but other than that they're all too content to be left to their own devices. It's not as if I'm not the kind to be a bad mother, not with such loving personality, am I? It's just how we are, and how we're brought up." |"Mmm... I love each and every one of the gookittens we made together, [pc.name]," Nihara purrs, her tails swaying in your direction. "Hearing their soft mewls when I hug them, or feeling them paw at my chest when they want to be nursed... so demanding, but I know they get that from you." Oh? And she thinks she's not demanding as well? But seriously, you're just glad that she's not regretting her decision in the least. "Hmm, I can't say I wasn't worried at first, allowing you to convince me to take the leap, [pc.name]. But at this point, there's no way I could ever imagine going back on all of this. "[nihara.isPregnant |Actually, with the way I'm feeling right now, I wouldn't mind being up for some more once I'm done with these buns in my oven..."
