rows.original:
"Getting tired of heavy words, are we? I'm not surprised." Nihara continues to hold you close as the both of you drift in lazy circles about the lake's center. "I'm glad that you took all of this in stride, [pc.name] — [nihara.isCorrupted
        |even my little jokes about keeping you here forever. Hope you didn't take those seriously, you'd be no good to me if I were to drown you in a fit of possessive madness."
        
        Well, when she lays it out like that... it's less reassuring than she probably intended, but the sentiment is appreciated. Then again, her being a little overbearing and scary is part and parcel of why you're still here, isn't it?
        |I was worried about how you'd react to all this. No doubt you're plenty famous and I'm not your only given that you travel all over like I did before putting down roots..."
        
        Would that bother her?
        
        "It doesn't matter, does it? Besides, if you really are that sought after by others... it does show that I've good taste to be able to get even a small piece of you, hmm?"
        
        Well, when she lays it out like that...it's a little blunt. There're many ways to approach the Tiran faith, and you guess someone like Nihara's bound to gravitate to fatalistic stoicism.
    ]
    
    The atmosphere falls silent again, and just as Nihara and you are about to settle in to take in the %"stars" upon the lake, the waters move — not the natural waves that pick up over the lake, but a gentle swelling and undulation of the surface, followed by the cool, gel-like sensation so familiar to your goocat. At first, you think it's Nihara teasing you with her hair and tails, but a little gasp from her makes it clear she's as surprised as you are. That gasp, though, soon becomes one of relief followed by a purr as the swells in the water reveal themselves to have distinctly feline ears.
    
    "Oh. I guess we were never really alone, [pc.name]. Although I do wonder how long the kittens have been listening in. They're still too young to really understand anything, but they know my voice, and clearly know yours too."
    
    One of the gookittens clambers onto your [pc.belly] and [pc.chest], leaving behind a sensation of what can only be described as cool wetness even beneath the water. As [nihara.isCorrupted
        |inky dark
        |azure
    ] as its mother, the little slime kitten is completely see-through, melding perfectly with the lake so long as it doesn't broach the surface. There're more of them in the water, tickling and nuzzling against you like housecats rubbing themselves against your legs, and Nihara lets out a lovely peal of laughter at the soft undulations in the water.
    
    "I didn't put them up to this, honest. But I'm not going to complain, and I don't think you are, either. Right, [pc.name]?"
    
    You just smile and try to pick up one of your gookittens, and it quite literally slips through your fingers, flowing through your grasp until it oozes right back into the lake. Nihara giggles at the sight, then gives you a little kiss.
    
    "Oh, the tales I have of how they are when you aren't around. They'll become more like me when they're older, [pc.name]. But it'll be several years yet... for now, though, let's enjoy the moment. Time will be upon us before we know it, and we'll look back upon these days as simpler times, silly as that might sound now."
    
    Nihara cuddles you while you take in the glinting cavern ceiling high above together. You've already spent a good while out here in the lake... which means there isn't that much longer before you've to pack it in. 
    
    But that just makes what time you do have with your goocat and the kittens all the more precious, doesn't it?
rows.translation:
真是受够了那些冗长的言辞，对吧？我一点也不感到意外。”尼原依然紧紧地抱着你，你们俩在湖中心缓缓地绕圈游动。“我很高兴你能如此冷静地面对这一切。 [pc.name] — [nihara.isCorrupted
        |就连我那些关于“永远把你留在身边”的玩笑，也希望你不要当真。如果我因为过度占有欲而把你淹没在疯狂之中，那你对我来说就毫无价值了……

嗯，当她这样直截了当地说出来时……其实并没有她想象中那么让人安心，不过我还是很感激她这份心意。话说回来，她那种有点强势又有点吓人的性格，不也正是你还在这里的原因之一吗？
        |我一直在担心你会如何看待这一切。毫无疑问，你已经非常有名了，而且我肯定也不是你唯一的朋友，毕竟你像我以前那样四处旅行，最终才安定下来……

这样的事情会让她感到困扰吗？
        
        没关系吧？而且，如果你真的那么受别人欢迎的话……能得到你的一点点，其实也说明我的眼光不错，嗯？”

嗯，当她这么说的时候。…这种方式有点过于直白了。对于提兰信仰，其实有很多不同的解读方式，而像尼哈拉这样的人，很自然地会倾向于那种宿命论式的 stoicism（斯多葛主义）。
    ]
    
    气氛再次陷入沉寂，就在尼哈拉和你准备仔细欣赏湖面上的那些“星星”时，水面开始波动——不是那种自然形成的涟漪，而是水面缓慢地起伏着，随后那种你那只小猫再熟悉不过的、凉爽而黏稠的感觉出现了。 起初，你以为尼哈拉是在用她的尾巴和毛发来逗弄你，但她发出的那声轻呼让你明白，她和你一样感到惊讶。然而，那声轻呼很快变成了松了一口气的声音，紧接着就是一声满足的呼噜声——因为水中的那些凸起物原来竟是猫一般的耳朵。
    
    哦，我想我们其实从来都没有真正地独处过。 [pc.name]虽然我在想这些小猫到底已经偷听了多久。它们还太小，根本不可能真正理解些什么，但它们认识我的声音，显然也认识你的声音。”

其中一只小猫爬上了你的肩膀…… [pc.belly] 以及 [pc.chest]这种感觉即便在水下也无法用其他词语来形容，只能称之为那种凉爽而湿润的感觉。 [nihara.isCorrupted
        |一片漆黑
        |azure
    ] 就像它的母亲一样，这只小黏液猫也是完全透明的，只要不浮到水面上，就能与湖水完美地融为一体。水里还有许多这样的小生物，它们会轻轻触碰你、依偎在你身边，就像家猫会蹭你的腿一样。尼哈拉看到水面上那些轻轻荡漾的波纹，忍不住发出一阵欢快的笑声。

“说实话，我并没有让它们这么做。但我也不会抱怨，我想你也不会吧？对吧？ [pc.name]你只是微笑着试图抓住其中一只小动物，但它真的从你的手指间溜走了，仿佛在你的手中流淌一般，最终又重新回到了湖里。尼哈拉看到这一幕，忍不住咯咯笑了起来，然后给了你一个轻吻。

“哦，关于你们不在的时候它们会变成什么样子，我可有很多故事呢……等它们长大一些，肯定会变得更像我吧。 [pc.name]不过那还需要几年的时间……不过现在，我们就先享受这段时光吧。不知不觉中，时间就会流逝，而当我们回首这些日子时，会觉得那些时光更加简单纯粹，尽管现在这么说可能听起来有些傻。”

尼原紧紧地抱着你，你们一起仰望着洞穴高高的天花板，那里闪烁着光芒。 你已经在湖边待了很长时间了……这意味着你剩下的时间已经不多了，很快就得停止这里的活动了。

不过，正因为如此，你与你的小猫们共度的这些时光就显得更加珍贵了，不是吗？
rows.raw:
"
    "Getting tired of heavy words, are we? I'm not surprised." Nihara continues to hold you close as the both of you drift in lazy circles about the lake's center. "I'm glad that you took all of this in stride, [pc.name] — [nihara.isCorrupted
        |even my little jokes about keeping you here forever. Hope you didn't take those seriously, you'd be no good to me if I were to drown you in a fit of possessive madness."
        
        Well, when she lays it out like that... it's less reassuring than she probably intended, but the sentiment is appreciated. Then again, her being a little overbearing and scary is part and parcel of why you're still here, isn't it?
        |I was worried about how you'd react to all this. No doubt you're plenty famous and I'm not your only given that you travel all over like I did before putting down roots..."
        
        Would that bother her?
        
        "It doesn't matter, does it? Besides, if you really are that sought after by others... it does show that I've good taste to be able to get even a small piece of you, hmm?"
        
        Well, when she lays it out like that...it's a little blunt. There're many ways to approach the Tiran faith, and you guess someone like Nihara's bound to gravitate to fatalistic stoicism.
    ]
    
    The atmosphere falls silent again, and just as Nihara and you are about to settle in to take in the %"stars" upon the lake, the waters move — not the natural waves that pick up over the lake, but a gentle swelling and undulation of the surface, followed by the cool, gel-like sensation so familiar to your goocat. At first, you think it's Nihara teasing you with her hair and tails, but a little gasp from her makes it clear she's as surprised as you are. That gasp, though, soon becomes one of relief followed by a purr as the swells in the water reveal themselves to have distinctly feline ears.
    
    "Oh. I guess we were never really alone, [pc.name]. Although I do wonder how long the kittens have been listening in. They're still too young to really understand anything, but they know my voice, and clearly know yours too."
    
    One of the gookittens clambers onto your [pc.belly] and [pc.chest], leaving behind a sensation of what can only be described as cool wetness even beneath the water. As [nihara.isCorrupted
        |inky dark
        |azure
    ] as its mother, the little slime kitten is completely see-through, melding perfectly with the lake so long as it doesn't broach the surface. There're more of them in the water, tickling and nuzzling against you like housecats rubbing themselves against your legs, and Nihara lets out a lovely peal of laughter at the soft undulations in the water.
    
    "I didn't put them up to this, honest. But I'm not going to complain, and I don't think you are, either. Right, [pc.name]?"
    
    You just smile and try to pick up one of your gookittens, and it quite literally slips through your fingers, flowing through your grasp until it oozes right back into the lake. Nihara giggles at the sight, then gives you a little kiss.
    
    "Oh, the tales I have of how they are when you aren't around. They'll become more like me when they're older, [pc.name]. But it'll be several years yet... for now, though, let's enjoy the moment. Time will be upon us before we know it, and we'll look back upon these days as simpler times, silly as that might sound now."
    
    Nihara cuddles you while you take in the glinting cavern ceiling high above together. You've already spent a good while out here in the lake... which means there isn't that much longer before you've to pack it in. 
    
    But that just makes what time you do have with your goocat and the kittens all the more precious, doesn't it?
    "

rows.original: Stepping up to the door, you knock and wait a little, but Nihara doesn't come to greet you. You try again, and when no response's forthcoming figure that she must be out either in the tunnels or visiting one of her few remaining clients holed up in their lakeshore villas... up until you hear her voice come from the rear of the little lake home. "[pc.name]? Is that you?" Oh, good. You thought she was out about her business. "I was going to make my rounds, but something told me to put it off today, and I guess it wasn't wrong. I'm out around the back — why don't you join me? It'll be a change of scenery from my sitting room for once." Seeing no reason to decline, you pad around the mushroom-wood boardwalks surrounding Nihara's home until you find the goocat herself out the back, as she said. There's a wide set of stairs that stop just short of the water's surface, and she's [nihara.isCorrupted |lounging on her side atop the lowest step, letting her hair and tails trail in the inky depths of the lake. That's one way to hydrate — as you get within hugging range, Nihara springs to her feet with shocking alacrity for a feline as large as her and moves to squeeze you fondly. "Oh, I'm so glad you decided to come home today, [pc.name]," she purrs. "I was just thinking about you." That's very nice and all, but maybe she could [pc.heightRange 72 |let up a little? You appreciate that she's glad to see you, but it feels like she's trying to crush you to pieces |pull back somewhat? As comfortable as this is, it's hard to breathe with her heavy, milky bosom smothering you ]. "Why? Don't you like it?" Nihara looks [pc.heightRange 72 | |down ]at you a moment, then eases her crushing bear hug. "All right, all right. But I am glad to see you — there's something you ought to know, [pc.name]." |sitting atop the lowest step, her legs and tails dipping into the water as she kicks at its surface and sparks motes of azure light to life, even for a brief moment. Seeing you approach, she shuffles to the side, making space for you beside her. "For visitors and goods from the temple who preferred to come by boat," Nihara explains. "Not that there're many of them these days. Hopefully the siege will be lifted soon and things will get back to normal... or as normal as they can be." But not for her. Nihara's life has changed so much that there's no going back to how things were, right? "Not when you came into my life." Your goocat splashes at the water with her bare feet, kicking up more motes of light; somewhere out in the lake are gookittens, young water wyrds at play... "But on that topic, I'm glad you decided to visit today, [pc.name]. I've been thinking, and it's kept me awake all night." Sounds serious. "Well..." Nihara bats at one of her goo-ears, and it melds momentarily into her azure slime-hair before popping up again. "It's a little silly and maybe also selfish, but I want to discuss it with you. You had some hand in this, and... well, you're also the only person who I can easily reach and trust to give me good advice all at once." ] And what would the matter be? Nihara says nothing, but plants her hands on [nihara.isPregnant |the firm roundness of her kitten bump |the slight, firm swell that her tummy has gained after having had your kittens ]. The both of you let the moment hang in the air, and you think you get where she's going with this... "Oh, haha. No, no — I know you're already on board with that, otherwise you wouldn't have put kittens into me to begin with. But our kittens do drink a lot, and I'm concerned that I might not have enough milk for them after [nihara.isPregnant |these are out of me |I've had several more ]." That's not too hard to solve — in fact, you think a potion pertaining to that problem was amongst your first introductions to Marches alchemy. If a hedge-witch in a small town like Ivris can do that, surely someone in Khor'minos can — "No alchemy." Hm? "I said, no alchemy." Nihara's lips set in a thin line and she folds her arms under her bosom as she pulls out her best displeased feline matron impression, which [nihara.isCorrupted |is very good given that she is one at this point |isn't very convincing, but it gets the point across ]. "You know what I am, what our kittens are. We're more fluid than most, and I'm not running the risk of it getting into my milk if I take something alchemical." You see. That does limit your options, but it does make sense. "My own mother warned me about it when I was on the cusp of womanhood," Nihara admits. "If it were easy, it wouldn't have kept me up all night and more." You'd thought the problem would be getting into Khor'minos to get an alchemist's services — that, you could have done. This, as Nihara points out, is trickier. "There're patrols who pass by the lake every so often — if a potion was all I needed, I could ask one of them to pick one up for me." She shakes her head. "[nihara.isCorrupted |How vexing, isn't it? As experienced as I may be, I have to admit that you're not bound to a source like I am |Things are always more complicated than they seem at first, but anyway! You're far more well-traveled than I am, [pc.name] ]. Seen anything out there that might help?"
rows.translation: 你走到门口，敲了敲门，稍等片刻，但尼原并没有来迎接你。你又试了一次，仍然没有得到任何回应，于是你猜想她肯定是在隧道里，或者是在去拜访那些还住在湖边别墅里的为数不多的客户……直到这时，你突然听到她的声音从那座小湖边的房子里传了出来。[pc.name]是你吗？” 哦，太好了。你还以为她去忙别的事情了呢。 “我本来打算去各处转转的，但突然觉得今天还是先别去了，看来我的决定没有错。我现在正在后院，你为什么不一起来呢？ 这总比一直待在客厅里要好，能换个环境吧。” 既然没有理由拒绝，你就沿着环绕尼哈拉家的蘑菇木栈道四处走，直到像她说的那样，在房子后面找到了那只高猫。 有一段宽阔的楼梯，它的尽头刚好位于水面上方，而她就站在那里。 [nihara.isCorrupted |她侧躺着坐在最底层的台阶上，让自己的毛发和尾巴垂落在湖水那漆黑的深处。这也是一种补充水分的方式呢——当你靠近到她能够触及的范围时，对于一只体型如此庞大的猫来说，尼哈拉会以惊人的敏捷速度站起身来，然后亲昵地过来抱你。 “哦，我真高兴你今天决定回家来。 [pc.name]我就是在想你呢，”她轻声说道。 这话听起来确实很贴心，不过或许她还可以…… [pc.heightRange 72 |能不能稍微放松一点？你当然应该感激她见到你时表现出的高兴，但她的态度看起来简直像是要把你压得粉身碎骨一样。 |稍微退后一点吧？虽然这样很舒服，但当她那沉重、乳白色的胸部压在身上时，确实让人有点喘不过气来。 ]为什么？你不喜欢吗？”尼原问道。 [pc.heightRange 72 | |向下 ]等一下，然后才松开了她那紧紧的拥抱。“好吧，好吧。但我…… 是 很高兴见到你——有件事你必须要知道。 [pc.name]." |她坐在最底层的台阶上，双腿和尾巴浸在水中，轻轻踢动水面，顿时迸发出阵阵蔚蓝色的轻型芒，虽然只持续了短短的瞬间。看到你走过来，她便往旁边挪了挪，为你腾出了位置。 这是为那些喜欢乘船前来的游客和从寺庙运出的货物准备的，”尼原解释道，“不过现在这样的人已经不多了。希望这次围困能尽快解除，一切都能恢复到正常状态……或者至少是尽可能接近正常的状态。但对她来说却不同。尼哈拉的生活已经发生了翻天覆地的变化，再也无法回到从前了，对吧？ “自从你出现在我的生活中之后，就再也不会了。”她赤着足部踩在水面上，溅起更多水花，那些水花在阳轻型下闪烁着轻型芒；而在湖的某处，一定有那些小水精灵们正在嬉戏玩耍。不过关于这个话题，我很高兴你今天决定来拜访我。 [pc.name]我一直在思考这个问题，甚至因此整晚都无法入睡。” 听起来挺严重的。 “嗯……”尼哈拉用手部指轻轻触碰着自己那根黏糊糊的耳朵，它瞬间融入她那蔚蓝色的黏液状头发中，又立刻重新冒了出来。“这个想法可能有点傻，甚至有点自私，但我还是想和你商量一下。你在这个事情中也起到了一定的作用，而且……嗯，你也是我唯一可以轻易联系到的人。 以及 希望你能立刻给我一些好的建议。 ] 那又有什么关系呢？ 尼原什么也没说，只是将双手部放在了…… [nihara.isPregnant |她那圆润的小肚子，显得格外可爱。 |生下你的小猫们后，她的肚子出现了那种轻微但明显的隆起。 ]你们俩让这一刻的气氛在空气中停留，你也在思考她这样做的意图是什么…… “哦，哈哈。不，不是的——我知道你已经同意我的想法了。 那个否则，你一开始也不会把我设定成能够哺育小猫的角色。不过我们的小猫确实喝很多奶，我担心之后我的奶可能不够给它们喝了。 [nihara.isPregnant |这些真的超出了我的能力范围。 |我还遇到了好几件类似的事情。 ]这其实并不难解决——事实上，你可能会认为，那些用于解决这类问题的药剂，正是你最初接触马奇斯炼金术时所学的内容。如果像伊夫里斯这样的小镇上的女巫都能做到这一点，那么在科尔米诺斯，肯定也有人能够做到…… “不需要炼金术。” 嗯？ “我说了，不需要炼金术。”尼哈拉的嘴唇紧抿成一条细线，她双臂交叉在胸前，摆出了那副极其不悦的猫娘模样…… [nihara.isCorrupted |考虑到她的情况，这已经非常不错了。 是 在这种情况下，只能选择一个方案了。 |虽然不是很有说服力，但至少把意思表达清楚了。 ]你知道我是什么，我们的小猫们也是什么。我们比大多数生物都更加灵活多变，所以如果我服用一些炼金药剂，也不会有这些药剂进入我的乳汁中，从而影响到小猫们。” 你看，这样的限制确实会缩小你的选择范围，但这也确实是有道理的。 在我即将成年时，我的母亲就警告过我这件事，”尼哈拉承认道，“如果这真的那么简单，就不会让我整夜无法入睡了。” 你可能会认为，问题应该在于如何进入科尔米诺斯去寻求炼金术士的帮助——毕竟，这个办法你是可以采用的。 正如尼原所指出的，这其实要棘手部一些。 “湖边偶尔会有巡逻队经过——如果只需要一瓶药水的话，我完全可以请他们中的某个人帮我去取来。”她摇了摇头，继续说道。[nihara.isCorrupted |真是让人恼火，不是吗？尽管我经验丰富，但我必须承认，你并不像我那样受限于某个特定的来源或限制。 |事情总是比乍看之下要复杂得多，不过无论如何！你经历的事情可比我多多了。 [pc.name] ]有没有看到什么可能有用的东西呢？

The second is to leave, as before, but with your eyes on theirs, letting them know, in no uncertain terms, that you see them. Opportunists are cowards. They wouldn't dare try to press if they knew that you could see them. Walking away with your eyes on them guarantees that they won't harass you as you try to leave. ] |If you were the type to try and jump someone, you'd probably do it in the dark, with no witnesses nearby, with your initial position veiled to your victim, on terrain that's uneven and unfamiliar to the victim, but familiar to yourself. You've learned to trust your gut over the years, and it hasn't led you wrong yet. You're being stalked. The question is, where is your stalker hiding...? You scan through the buildings, carefully taking in every detail that you can see in the dim light of the Undermountain. Rotten windows; dilapidated doors; sagging roofs and walls; torn up floors and roads– One building catches your eye. A glint of something almost metallic, the sheen of the cave stone's lights hitting off it just the right way that you pick it up. You stare in that direction... and in the swallowing blackness of the cave around you, you pick out a pair of rubies. No, not rubies. Eyes. Eyes, sparkling red in the blackness, staring you down from the comfort of their abode, with black, vertical slits for pupils. Close enough that they could strike you, but far enough away that they'd need the element of surprise to do it. The eyes are crouched low to the ground, peering just barely over some debris lining the doorway to a rundown shack, trying to remain hidden – maybe they think you don't see them. There are two ways you could handle this. The first is to turn your back – let them believe that they still have the element of surprise. If they're a mugger, they'll try to jump you the second you turn around, but you have the advantage of knowing. It would be easy to turn the advantage to yourself. They wouldn't dare try to press if they knew that you could see them. Walking away with your eyes on them guarantees that they won't harass you as you try to leave. ] ]
rows.translation: [flags.RAIZEL_COMBAT |和之前一样，当你走在这条废弃且腐朽的街道上时，会有一种令人不安的感觉……仿佛有什么东西存在于周围。你独自一人在这里，但空气中确实弥漫着某种气息——那种气息会让你感到不安，甚至让你觉得，黑暗之中，隐藏着比表面看起来更复杂的东西。 这种不安感更甚了，因为你之前就已经来过这里，俗话说，一次被咬，就会变得胆小谨慎。 你环顾四周，盯着那些破败的建筑物和散落一地的杂物，试图寻找任何能够证实或缓解你心中不安的东西。 [pc.cunningRange 0 60 |[pc.presenceRange 0 60 |不，你确信那里肯定有什么东西。你知道如何让自己被注意到，你也知道该怎么做才能达到这个目的。 隐藏 没错，上次你的直觉是对的，而你从中得到的教训就是：应该更经常相信自己的直觉。 现在，你又感觉有人在跟踪你。你非常确信这一点。如果你的猜测没错的话，那么很可能会…… 你转过身去，果然，在那逐渐笼罩而来的黑暗中，有一双宝石般红润的眼睛，那眼睛上有着垂直的裂隙，正在黑暗中闪烁着光芒，直直地注视着你。然而，你仍然无法清楚地看到那双眼睛所属的生物究竟是什么。 它们的距离近到足以让它们一跃就能攻击你，但同时又远到它们必须先跃起来才能发动攻击，而这正好给了你足够的反应时间。 他们能够看到你，但现在，你也能看到他们了。如果他们还是像之前那样打算从背后袭击你，那么他们就失去了这个优势。 面对这种情况，你有两种选择。第一种就是转过身去——让他们以为他们仍然拥有突然袭击的优势。如果他们是劫匪，那么当你转身的瞬间，他们就会试图袭击你，但你知道他们的意图，因此很容易将这个优势转化为自己的优势。 第二种方法也是像之前那样离开，但要在他们注意你的时候这么做，要让他们清楚地知道你看到了他们。机会主义者都是胆小鬼——如果他们知道你能看到他们，就绝不敢试图继续骚扰你。在他们注视着你的情况下离开，就能确保你在试图离开时不会遭到他们的骚扰。 ] |你比他们聪明。要想占上风，还需要更多的狡猾手段才行。 你又在被人跟踪了。你确信自己是这样。如果你的判断没错，那么很可能会…… 你转过身去，果然，在那逐渐降临的漆黑中，有一双宝石般红润的眼睛，那眼睛上有着垂直的裂隙，正在暗影中闪烁着轻型芒，直直地盯着你的眼睛。然而，你仍然无法清楚地看到那双眼睛所属的生物究竟是什么。 它们的距离近到足以让它们一跃就能攻击你，但同时又远到必须先跃起来才能发动攻击，因此你有足够的时间做出反应。 |沿着这座曾经热闹非凡的前哨小镇的废墟前行，你不禁会感到一丝……不安。所有的建筑都空无一人，这里似乎已经很久没有人来了。穿越幽暗的山腹地带非常危险，就连盗贼和强盗也不会敢来到这里——你也不会在这里遇到这类人吧？ 一种熟悉的不安感逐渐从你的脊背蔓延开来，最终停留在你的脖颈后方。 [pc.cunningRange 0 60 |[pc.presenceRange 0 60 不，不是红宝石。而是眼睛——在黑暗中闪烁着红色的光芒，从它们藏身的地方凝视着你，它们的瞳孔是黑色的、呈垂直状的裂隙。那些眼睛离你足够近，足以向你发起攻击；但同时又离你足够远，因此需要出其不意才能真正伤到你。它们低低地趴在地上，仅仅从一间破旧小屋门口堆积的杂物后面探出头来，试图隐藏自己——也许它们以为你根本看不到它们。 rows.original: Your intuition says one thing, but your senses say another. Maybe pausing to consider your next action would be prudent. You are certainly going to be jumped if you do this.
rows.translation: 你的直觉告诉你一个答案，但你的感官却告诉你另一个方向。或许，暂停片刻，仔细考虑一下下一步该怎么做，会是个明智的选择。 你就是…… 当然 如果你这么做，肯定会惹上麻烦的。
rows.raw: "Your intuition says one thing, but your senses say another. Maybe pausing to consider your next action would be prudent.\n\nYou are certainly going to be jumped if you do this."

rows.original: With any luck, whoever, or whatever, is watching you is just territorial and wants you to leave without a fuss.
rows.translation: 但愿，那些正在监视你的人，只是出于领地意识，想让你安静地离开而已。
rows.raw: "With any luck, whoever, or whatever, is watching you is just territorial and wants you to leave without a fuss."

rows.original: Turning your back will invite conflict, but you'll have the advantage of knowing that it's coming.
rows.translation: 转身离开 会引发冲突不过，你知道它即将到来，这一点会让你占据优势。
rows.raw: "Turning your back will invite conflict, but you'll have the advantage of knowing that it's coming."

rows.original: Walk backward while facing forward, letting your stalker know that you see them. There is no way they would try to engage you without the element of surprise.
rows.translation: 向前走的同时向后退，让跟踪你的人知道你发现了他们。如果没有突然性，他们是绝不会试图与你交战的。
rows.raw: "Walk backward while facing forward, letting your stalker know that you see them. There is no way they would try to engage you without the element of surprise."

rows.original: You pause as indecision racks you and you try to process the different options available to you. You could call out: if someone is out there, yelling might get them scared to approach. But if there isn't, you'd be drawing the attention of everything in the cave towards you. You remain still on the cobblestone road, holding your ground. Whatever it is that's out there – if, indeed, anything at all – you refuse to show them that you're scared. You're not, of course. But they need to know that you're not. There's just the littlest of disturbances in the air around you as wait. A shifting of stone against stone, the dust shuffling in the air around you. The tiniest of clicks resonates against the stone walls of the caves, echoing into the distance. The silence is simultaneously all-consuming, and all-telling. One sound, no louder than the rest, suddenly stands out among the ambience: something large and sinuous, grinding against the rocks in long, continuous, fluid motions. It's hard to pinpoint exactly where it's coming from– The air whirls around you, suddenly yanking on your senses, causing you to pivot. It's hard to see in the darkness, and the creature's camouflage is excellent, but there's no denying something obvious: two ruby red eyes, gleaming almost brilliantly despite the darkness, split by pitch-black vertical slits. You can't make out the details of the creature it's attached to, but you can tell that it's huge. How something that big got so close to you is... well, [silly |a skill issue |maybe you need to work on your observational skills ]. The assailant recognizes that now is the time to strike, now that you've seen it. Before you have the chance to raise your arms in defense, it's upon you!
rows.translation: 你陷入犹豫之中，试图权衡各种可行的选择。你可以大声呼喊——如果有人在那里的话，这样的喊声可能会把他们吓跑，使他们不敢靠近。但如果没有人的话，你的喊声只会把洞穴里所有的注意力都引向你。 你依然站在那条铺满鹅卵石的道路上，坚守着自己的位置。无论外面有什么——如果真的有什么存在的话——你都拒绝让他们看出你害怕了。当然，你并不害怕。但他们必须知道你并不害怕。 在等待的过程中，你周围的空气中会传来一些细微的声响——石头相互碰撞发出的声音，空气中悬浮的尘埃轻轻晃动所发出的声响，还有那些极其微小的咔嗒声，在洞穴的石壁间回荡，逐渐远去。 这种沉默既令人窒息，又透露出一切。 在周围的嘈杂声中，突然有一种声音凸显了出来——那是一种沉重而蜿蜒的声音，物体在岩石上不断地、连续地、流畅地摩擦着。很难准确判断这个声音是从哪里传来的…… 空气在你周围旋转，突然猛烈地冲击着你的感官，迫使你迅速转向。在黑暗中很难看清周围的情况，而那个生物的伪装能力也非常出色，但有一个显而易见的事实是无法忽视的：那两只宝石般红润的眼睛，在黑暗中依然闪烁着耀眼的光芒，而它们的眼眶中间则被一道漆黑的竖状裂口分隔开来。 你无法看清它所附着在的那个生物的细节，但可以确定的是…… 巨大的像那样巨大的东西能够如此接近你，实在……嗯，真是令人难以置信。 [silly |这是技术上的问题。 |也许你需要提升一下自己的观察能力了。 ]攻击者知道，现在正是发动攻击的最佳时机——既然你已经看到了它，那么在你还有机会举起手臂进行防御之前，攻击就会降临到你身上！
rows.raw: " You pause as indecision racks you and you try to process the different options available to you. You could call out: if someone is out there, yelling might get them scared to approach. But if there isn't, you'd be drawing the attention of everything in the cave towards you. You remain still on the cobblestone road, holding your ground. Whatever it is that's out there – if, indeed, anything at all – you refuse to show them that you're scared. You're not, of course. But they need to know that you're not. There's just the littlest of disturbances in the air around you as wait. A shifting of stone against stone, the dust shuffling in the air around you. The tiniest of clicks resonates against the stone walls of the caves, echoing into the distance. The silence is simultaneously all-consuming, and all-telling. One sound, no louder than the rest, suddenly stands out among the ambience: something large and sinuous, grinding against the rocks in long, continuous, fluid motions. It's hard to pinpoint exactly where it's coming from– The air whirls around you, suddenly yanking on your senses, causing you to pivot. It's hard to see in the darkness, and the creature's camouflage is excellent, but there's no denying something obvious: two ruby red eyes, gleaming almost brilliantly despite the darkness, split by pitch-black vertical slits. You can't make out the details of the creature it's attached to, but you can tell that it's huge. How something that big got so close to you is... well, [silly |a skill issue |maybe you need to work on your observational skills ]. The assailant recognizes that now is the time to strike, now that you've seen it. Before you have the chance to raise your arms in defense, it's upon you! "

rows.original: [flags.RAIZEL_COMBAT |You've been over this before with this territorial mugger, and your encounter with them is going to go the way you want it to this time. You're not afraid of conflict, especially when the advantage is now yours. You turn your back on them, feigning like you've given up the staring competition, and resume your walk down the abandoned street of the minoan outpost. If your attacker is dumb enough to try, they'll think that now is the time, and they'll go for it – but you're ready for that. The sound of something large and sinuous rolling over stone and dirt meets your ears, as opposed to footfalls, however light, of, well, someone with feet. You have to rely on your instincts more than your eyes for this[flags.ZO_GIFT|, but thanks to some particular training from a certain monk, your senses are honed as sharp as any blade|, but your vision wasn't going to be your strongest asset in these caves anyway]. When the sound gets loud enough and you feel the wind start to bristle against your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun], you swing with your [pc.weapon] – and it makes contact with something thick and fleshy, causing a loud, pained grunt to echo through the air. This isn't your first dance with this mugger. They flail a bit from the pain, but, as you expected, the moment they recover, they'd rather resume the fight than attempt to flee! |Not only are you not afraid of conflict, you're confident enough in your abilities – and in the advantage that you have – that you're going to turn your back on your assailant. If they try to strike, it would be easy to turn their advantage to yours. So, you do. You turn around and continue your path down the neglected and dilapidated roads of the Undermountain. Your gait is casual, but your footfalls are light: you keep your ears peeled for any sound of your attacker approaching. You're not surprised when they do, although the sound is unusual. You expected footfalls as someone runs towards you: what you hear is something large and sinuous, grinding against the rocks in long, continuous, fluid motions[var0|. A veparus, maybe? Whatever the case,|. It's certainly not bipedal, but whatever the case,] it's coming at you, fast. It's a simple matter of baiting them until they get close, then drawing your [pc.weapon] and striking when they think the moment is theirs. You're relying on your ears and your instincts more than your eyes, but[flags.ZO_GIFT|, thanks to some particular training from a certain monk, your senses are honed as sharp as any blade| your vision wasn't going to be your strongest asset in these caves anyway]. With a swing, your [pc.weapon] makes contact with something thick and fleshy, causing a loud, pained grunt to echo through the air. You turn to face your assailant[var1|[var0|: a veparus, as you had guessed|they have a long, thick, serpentine body, gleaming with darkened black-and-blue scales], but where you had assumed they would have a more humanoid visage, their head is more akin to a snake's| although it's difficult to make out the specifics of your attacker, you can at least tell that they don't have a more ‘conventional' lower body and have the form of a large snake]. But you don't have the time to get a more thorough appraisal: it's fight or flee, and with their posturing as they regain their composure, they're choosing to fight! ]

rows.original:
... so you're not going to. You put one foot in front of the other at a faster clip, beating the dust off the cobblestone as you get out of there. The sooner you're gone, the sooner you don't have to worry about getting assaulted in the dark, where you're at a constant, natural disadvantage.
    
    Thankfully, your strategy of ‘getting the hell out of there' works out. The coarse, uneven stone walls of the cave blend together as you walk, but you don't have that feeling in your gut that you're being stalked any more. Choosing to leave was the safer play.
    
    Who knows if you'll be this lucky every time you walk through shit shithole, though.
rows.translation:
所以你不会去的。你会快步前行，脚步声在鹅卵石上回响，尽快离开那里。你越快离开，就越不用担心在暗影中遭到袭击——在那种环境中，你始终处于劣势。
    
    幸运的是，你“尽快离开那里”的策略果然奏效了。当你走在洞穴里时，那些粗糙而不平整的石壁让人难以分辨方向，但你现在再也没有那种被跟踪的感觉了。 选择离开才是更安全的做法。

不过，谁知道每次你遇到这种糟糕的情况时，是否还能这么幸运呢？

rows.original:
With your eyes firmly locked onto the ruby-red pair hidden in the darkness of the rotten, dilapidated buildings, you put one foot behind the other, continuing down your path while letting your would-be stalker know, in no uncertain terms, that you see them. The very fact that they used the cover of darkness to mask their intent means that they had hoped to use it to their advantage, and now that that's gone, they would be foolhardy to try and approach you now.
    
    As you thought, the ruby-red eyes remain fixated on yours in turn, but they do not attempt to pursue. Whoever, or whatever, it is in the inky-black remains in place until, eventually, the distance between you two is great enough that you lose them. You keep your ears peeled at the sound of anything approaching you from any angle, but there's nothing. You're alone.
    
    If this is their territory, then you'll no doubt encounter them again at some point. But, hopefully, next time will go just as smoothly as this time did.
rows.translation:
你的目光紧紧锁定在那对隐藏在那些破败不堪、阴暗潮湿的建筑中的红宝石般鲜红的物体上，你一步接一步地继续前行，同时明确无误地向那些可能正在跟踪你的人表明：你看到了他们。 他们利用黑暗来掩盖自己的意图，这一事实本身就说明他们原本希望借此获得优势；而现在这个机会已经消失，如果他们现在还试图接近你，那未免太愚蠢了。

正如你所想的，那双红宝石般的眼睛依然紧紧地盯着你，但他们并没有采取任何行动来接近你。 无论那是什么，它始终静静地待在原地，直到你们之间的距离变得足够大，以至于你再无法看到它。你时刻保持着警惕，试图捕捉任何从任何方向靠近你的声音，但最终什么也没有。 你孤身一人。

如果这里是他们的地盘，那么毫无疑问，你迟早会再次遇到他们。不过，希望下次一切都能像这次一样顺利。

"
    With your eyes firmly locked onto the ruby-red pair hidden in the darkness of the rotten, dilapidated buildings, you put one foot behind the other, continuing down your path while letting your would-be stalker know, in no uncertain terms, that you see them.     "

rows.original: With that final blow, the large, snake-like assailant flops backward, wrangling and reeling from the pain of the strike. It lets out a long, haggard hiss before rolling onto its stomach. The red eyes give you one final look, piercing into yours through the dim light of the cave, before the creature turns around and slithers away as quickly as it can, having recognized that the fight hasn't gone its way.[var0 | You watch as it slithers; it heads towards a nearby embankment of discarded rubble before sharply turning, following the path through the Undermountain. Based on its direction, it looks like it's heading towards the nearest Waystone. You've encountered it often enough now that maybe it's time you got the drop on it. ] You remain in your combat-ready stance for a short time, waiting for a surprise attack that never comes. Silence – true, unlimited silence – replaces the bustle and hectic ambience of combat, and is not underscored by the potential of a stalker looking for an easy mark. This fight is over.
rows.translation: 随着那一记致命一击，那只体型庞大、形似蛇的攻击者向后仰倒，因剧痛而不断挣扎、翻滚。它发出一声长长的、充满痛苦的嘶嘶声，随后翻到了腹部。那双红色的眼睛在洞穴昏暗的轻型线中再次注视着你，仿佛要穿透你的视线。最终，这个生物意识到这场战斗并没有如它所愿地发展，便以最快的速度滑走了。[var0 | 你看着它蜿蜒前行，它朝着附近的一处堆满废弃碎石的土堤方向移动，然后突然转向，沿着一条小路穿过了地下山脉。根据它的移动方向来看…… 看起来它正朝着最近的路标石方向移动。你现在已经遇到这种情况太多次了，或许是时候采取行动了。 你 抢先一步抓住了机会。 ] 你保持着战斗准备姿势站立了一小会儿，等待着那次从未到来的突然袭击。寂静——真正的、无边无际的寂静——取代了战斗中那种喧嚣与紧张的气氛，也没有任何潜伏者正在寻找容易攻击的目标这样的潜在威胁。这场战斗，已经结束了。

rows.original:
Unfortunately for you, there are simply too many factors against you. You never could get a clear, easy look at your assailant. This is their territory. The footing is uneven. The lighting is piss poor. [var0
        |Even with knowing that you were under attack and opening the fight with the advantage, you were simply overwhelmed.
        |Your opponent opened the fight you just couldn't manage to recover from.
    ]
    
    Darkness overtakes you...
rows.translation:
对你来说，不幸的是，有太多不利因素在阻碍你。你根本无法清楚地看清袭击者是谁。这里可是他们的地盘，地面凹凸不平，光线也极其昏暗。 [var0
        |尽管你知道自己正处于攻击之下，并且是以优势开始了这场战斗，但你还是被彻底压倒了。
        |你的对手发起了攻击，而你根本无法恢复过来。
    ]
    
    黑暗将你吞噬……

"
    Unfortunately for you, there are simply too many factors against you. You never could get a clear, easy look at your assailant. This is their territory. The footing is uneven. The lighting is piss poor. [var0
        |Even with knowing that you were under attack and opening the fight with the advantage, you were simply overwhelmed.
        |Your opponent opened the fight you just couldn't manage to recover from.
    ]
    
    Darkness overtakes you...
    "

rows.original: ... and when you awake, darkness remains. You pull yourself up into a sitting position. Your body aches all over, not the least of reasons why being the quality of your ‘mattress'. But... you're in one piece. Your assailant is nowhere to be seen. They just... beat you up, and left you there on the road. You grunt and groan, shakily pulling yourself to your feet. Whatever it was that attacked you, it didn't want you dead. After checking yourself over for any permanent damage, and finding nothing, the next thing to check is your purse. If it had any reason to attack you at all, it was either because you had entered its territory and it wanted you gone... or because it wanted your money. Or both. And, yep. There are fewer coins in there. You don't need to count every coin to know that for certain.[var0 | With your stiff and sore muscles singing in agony, you try and rack your brain for strategies on how to deal with that thing the next time you run into it. Or, more appropriately, it runs into you. It always stalks you from behind; it always seems to know your path through the caves... If both of those are true, maybe you should try and kite it towards the nearest Waystone. It's close to the mouth of the cave, so natural light will have an easier time reaching in, even in the dark of night. And, if worse comes to worse, you'll have three different ways of escaping. ] You're a little frustrated in yourself for having lost the fight, but at least you're leaving the area with your life. All you can really do is promise yourself that next time will go differently.
rows.translation: ……当你醒来时，周围依然是一片暗影。 你挣扎着坐起来，全身都疼得厉害，这大概也是你的“床垫”质量太差的原因吧……不过，你至少没有受伤，袭击你的那个人也不见踪影。 他们只是……把你打了一顿，然后把你丢在路边。 你哼哼着，摇摇晃晃地站了起来。不管是什么东西袭击了你，它显然并不想置你于死地。 在检查自己是否受了任何永久性的伤害，确认没有问题之后，接下来要检查的就是你的钱包了。 如果它真的有理由攻击你，那要么是因为你进入了它的领地，它想让你离开……要么就是因为它想要你的钱。或者两者都是原因。 没错，里面的硬币确实少了。你不需要数每一枚硬币就能确定这一点。[var0 | 当你的肌肉僵硬且酸痛得令人难以忍受时，你会绞尽脑汁思考下次遇到那种东西时该如何应对。或者，更准确地说，应该是那种东西总是先找到你。它总是从背后悄悄接近你；似乎总是能预知你在洞穴中的行进路线…… 如果这两点都是事实的话…… 也许你应该试着把它引向最近的路标石那里。它位于洞穴的入口附近，因此即使在深夜，自然光也能更容易地照进洞内。而且，如果情况变得糟糕，你还有三种不同的逃生途径。 ] 虽然输掉了这场战斗，你内心难免会感到有些沮丧，但至少你还能活着离开这个地方。你现在能做的，就是告诉自己：下次一定要做得不同。
rows.raw: " ... and when you awake, darkness remains. You pull yourself up into a sitting position. Your body aches all over, not the least of reasons why being the quality of your ‘mattress'. But... you're in one piece. Your assailant is nowhere to be seen. They just... beat you up, and left you there on the road. You grunt and groan, shakily pulling yourself to your feet. Whatever it was that attacked you, it didn't want you dead. After checking yourself over for any permanent damage, and finding nothing, the next thing to check is your purse. If it had any reason to attack you at all, it was either because you had entered its territory and it wanted you gone... or because it wanted your money. Or both. And, yep. There are fewer coins in there. You don't need to count every coin to know that for certain.[var0 | With your stiff and sore muscles singing in agony, you try and rack your brain for strategies on how to deal with that thing the next time you run into it. Or, more appropriately, it runs into you. It always stalks you from behind; it always seems to know your path through the caves... If both of those are true, maybe you should try and kite it towards the nearest Waystone. It's close to the mouth of the cave, so natural light will have an easier time reaching in, even in the dark of night. And, if worse comes to worse, you'll have three different ways of escaping. ] You're a little frustrated in yourself for having lost the fight, but at least you're leaving the area with your life. All you can really do is promise yourself that next time will go differently. "

rows.original: You [raizel.winCount 0 2 |nervously continue your pace down this path. You're only a stone's throw from the opening to the Undermountain's mouth; far enough away that, if you're jumped by that long, sinuous monster again, you might be able to beat a hasty retreat. You've [raizel.winCount 0 1 |never actually won a fight against it |rarely come out ahead against it ] and although it's left you alive every time, it... hurts. And it keeps robbing you. |confidently stride down this path, your gait upright and casual. You know that the large, sinuous monster that you sometimes encounter has made its territory here in the caves, but you've proven yourself capable of handling it. [raizel.winCount 3 5 |Sometimes you lost the fight, even when you had the advantage, but honestly? That just makes it more interesting. The fact that it keeps taking your money means that it's intelligent enough to understand its value, meaning it makes for an entertaining challenge. |More than capable, really: you've come out on top every single time. The fact that it kept falling for your feint and giving you the advantage tells you that you're probably not dealing with something all that intelligent, to be frank. ] ] And... speak of the devil. Crossing the pounded cobblestone road ahead of you is a long, sinuous creature, slithering from one side to the other. It initially doesn't notice you, but when you suddenly pause your footfalls, it looks in your direction. The familiar ruby-red eyes, gleaming in the dark of the cave with the little bit of lighting it offers, is the only telltale sign you need. Unlike all the other times you've encountered it, this time is different, for a lot of reasons. You're both in the middle of the road, whereas before, it preferred to hide in the shadows and strike when it thought it had the advantage. And, following that train of thought, when it sees you and you see it, it doesn't make any effort to attack. [raizel.winCount 0 2 |In fact, after acknowledging who you are, it simply... leaves. Like you're not worth the time or effort to engage with you again. To be honest, given your win record against it, you're sort of glad. It slithers at a somewhat-casual pace across the street and into the ramshackle abode that it calls its nest. |After giving you one look, it lowers its head and turns away, like an embarrassed lover encountering an ex in public. It quickly slithers across the road towards the ramshackle abode it calls its nest without giving you another look. ] A thought crosses your mind. Maybe you should follow it. On the one hand, it's been the one to engage with you. You always gave it every opportunity to not attack, and it always went after you, perhaps because it was territorial, or... well, any infinite number of reasons, really. Going after it might just provoke it further. You don't even know if it's intelligent enough to speak. On the other, it's clearly not interested in fighting right now, or, perhaps, any more at all, [raizel.winCount 0 3 |having gotten used to your presence and recognizing that you're not much of a threat. Maybe it'll be more amenable to a friendly approach |now that you've proven that you can win no matter the terrain or circumstance. Maybe it'll be willing to speak now that it knows that fighting isn't a winning strategy ]. At the same time, it is, at best, a homeless [var0 |veparus |person ], or, at worst, an animal. Leaving well enough alone is a valid strategy, too.
rows.translation: 你 [raizel.winCount 0 2 |你紧张地继续沿着这条小路前行。距离通往山腹深域入口的地方已经不远了；不过这个距离还算足够，因为如果那头身形修长、行动敏捷的怪物再次突然袭击你，你应该还有时间迅速撤退。你…… [raizel.winCount 0 1 |实际上从未赢得过与它的战斗。 |面对这种情况，很少有人能够取得胜利。 ] 虽然每次它都让你活下来，但……这真的很痛苦。而且它还在不断地剥夺你的东西。 |你自信地沿着这条道路前行，步伐从容而坚定。你知道，那些偶尔会遇到的巨大、蜿蜒曲折的怪物已经将这里洞穴作为它们的领地，但你也证明了自己有能力应对它们。 [raizel.winCount 3 5 |有时候，即使你处于优势地位，也还是会输掉这场“战斗”。但说实话，这反而让整个过程变得更加有趣。既然它总是会“抢走”你的钱，那就说明它足够“聪明”，能够理解金钱的价值——因此，它确实构成了一个充满挑战性的、有趣的体验。 |其实你完全有能力做到：每次你都能取得胜利。事实上，那个对手总是会上当受骗，从而给你带来优势，这恰恰说明，坦白说，你面对的其实并不是什么特别聪明的对手。 ] ] 而且……说起来正好碰巧。 在你前方，那条被踩得坑坑洼洼的鹅卵石路上，有一条长长的、蜿蜒曲折的生物正在来回滑动。它起初并没有注意到你，但当你突然停下脚步时，它便朝你的方向看了过来。 那双熟悉的宝石红眼睛，在洞穴昏暗的光线中闪烁着微弱的光芒，这就是你所需要的唯一线索。 与以往你遇到的所有情况不同，这一次却有很多不同之处。 你们现在都处于同样的处境中，而之前，它总是喜欢隐藏在暗处，等到认为自己占上风时才会发动攻击。按照这种思维方式，当它看到你，你也看到它的时候，它就不会再试图发动攻击了。 [raizel.winCount 0 2 |事实上，一旦它认出了你的身份，就会直接……离开。就好像你根本不值得它再花时间和精力与你打交道。说实话，考虑到你之前与它的对战记录，你反而会感到有些庆幸。它会以一种相当随意的方式穿过街道，然后钻进那座破败不堪的住所——那里就是它所谓的“巢穴”。 |它只是看了你一眼，就立刻低下头转开了身，就像一个在公共场合遇到前恋人的尴尬恋人一样。它迅速地爬过马路，朝着那个它称之为巢穴的破旧居所跑去，再也没有回头看你一眼。 ] 你突然想到了某个想法。或许你应该追随它。 一方面，正是这个想法一直在与你互动。你始终给了它一切机会去展现自己。 不是 它会攻击你，而且总是追着你不放，也许是因为它有领地意识，或者……其实，原因可能有无数种。去招惹它反而可能会让它更加恼火。你甚至不知道它是否有足够的智力来理解人类的语言。 另一方面，很明显，它现在并没有战斗的意愿，或者说，也许它根本就不再有兴趣战斗了。 [raizel.winCount 0 3 |已经习惯了你的存在，并且意识到你并不会构成什么威胁。或许，用友好的方式去接近它会更容易取得成功。 |既然你已经证明了无论在何种地形或环境下你都能取得胜利，那么现在它或许会愿意开口说话了——因为它知道，战斗并不是获胜的途径。 ]同时，它充其量也只是一个没有家可归的东西罢了。 [var0 |维帕鲁斯 |人物 ]或者，最糟糕的情况下，被当作动物来对待。选择不干涉、让事情保持原状，也是一种可行的策略。

rows.original:
You don't know who or what it is. All you really know is that it's tried to jump you multiple times, now. It's opportunistic and underhanded. Leaving it be is the better call.
        
        But... if you ever wanted to, the option is there. You doubt that it's going anywhere. It'll be better to have more friends than enemies – or, at the least, more people and things you understand than you don't.
rows.translation:
你根本不知道它到底是谁，也不知道它究竟是什么。你现在所知道的，只是它已经多次试图攻击你。这种生物既机会主义又阴险狡诈，因此放任它不管才是更好的选择。

不过……如果你真的想采取行动的话，这个选项也是存在的。你大概也怀疑它不会跑到哪里去吧。拥有更多的朋友总比拥有更多的敌人要好——或者说，至少，拥有更多你能够理解的人或事物，总比面对那些你无法理解的东西要好。

        You don't know who or what it is. All you really know is that it's tried to jump you multiple times, now. It's opportunistic and underhanded. Leaving it be is the better call.

        "

rows.original:
Occasionally, you'd encounter a long, sinuous creature somewhere in the Undermountain, and it'd try to mark you as easy prey by getting the jump on you in the darkness. But, one time recently, you saw each other on this road, and after that, it never attempted to fight you again, [raizel.winCount 0 2
        |probably because you're not worth the effort. Which, frankly, you don't mind. Fights against it, uh, didn't really go your way
        |probably because it knows it's not worth the effort. You put up way too much of a fight for what is supposed to be an easy mark. Fights rarely went its way, no matter what advantage it had
    ].
    
    Ever since then, though, it hasn't tried to fight you a single time. Whatever the reason, it simply... left you be, ever since that moment.
    
    Odds are, it's probably still living in its nest: inside one of the rundown, crummy buildings lining the road, a symbol of the area's history as a minoan outpost. You wouldn't be surprised if it's still aware of you every time you pass through the area. If you wanted, you could investigate the buildings to try and seek it out. Maybe trying to understand it could help you, well, avoid further confrontations in the future.
    
    Alternatively, you could leave well enough alone.
rows.translation:
偶尔，在幽暗的地底深处，你会遇到那种身形修长、行动诡异的生物。它们总会试图在黑暗中突然袭击你，将你视为容易捕获的猎物。然而，最近有那么一次，在这条路上，你们再次相遇了，从那以后，它们再也没有试图与你交战过。 [raizel.winCount 0 2
        |大概是因为你根本不值得别人费这个劲。说实话，你对此也毫不在意。不过，与这种想法的抗争，嗯，结果并不如你所愿。
        |大概是因为它知道这样做并不值得。对于一个本应轻而易举就能得到的目标，你却投入了太多的精力去抗争。无论它拥有多少优势，这些抗争几乎从未让它如愿以偿。
    ]但从那以后，它再也没有试图与你争斗过。无论出于什么原因，从那一刻起，它就……不再打扰你了。

很可能，它现在仍然生活在它的巢穴里：就在路边那些破旧不堪的建筑物之中，而这些建筑物恰恰见证了这片地区曾经作为米诺斯前哨站的历史。 每次你经过那个区域时，如果它仍然能察觉到你的存在，你也不会感到惊讶。如果你愿意，可以仔细调查那些建筑物，试着找到它。或许，尝试了解它的本质，能够帮助你避免将来再次与它发生冲突。
    
    或者，你也可以选择什么都不做，让一切保持原样。

rows.original: This is uncharted territory, but you take the chance and make your way towards the one building that you watched the creature slip into. This time, it's you intruding on it. You can't begin to guess how this is going to go, but [raizel.winCount 0 2 |if it didn't attack you when it had the chance – albeit, in the more broad ‘light' of the street, where it couldn't sneak-attack you – then you want to believe that it won't attack you again this time |given that it didn't attack you when it could have, it's come to understand that violence isn't worthwhile. Then again, it might still lash out to protect its nest, but if that's the case, you'll retreat, and your lesson will be learned ]. You cross the threshold from the building's only doorframe – the door itself still on the hinges, but it looks like it hasn't opened or closed in an age – and peer into its darkness. "Hello?" you call into the abyss. At first, no response. Then, a pair of ruby-red eyes, bright enough to pierce the veil. They materialize into being from seemingly nothing at all. As soon as they open, they focus directly onto you, as if they had been watching you from the very start. The eyes meet you at eye-level[pc.heightRange 0 84 | |, telling you that, whatever it is, it's very tall ]. You can't see any other part of it in the darkness – whatever it's wearing, the camouflage is very well done. "[raizel.winCount 0 2 |What do you want?" it asks. |Go away," it says disdainfully ]. From the sound of its voice, it's feminine, albeit on the lower, gruffer side. It's the kind of voice that you'd hear at a seedier, less reputable bar, one that someone might frequent a little too often. At least you're not chasing some animal. You have a few options on how you want to respond. The first is the easiest, simplest, and straightest way forward: you tell her that you just want to talk. She's assailed you several times and all you want to know is why. Keeping it simple could be an easy way to open up to it. It? You presume she's a ‘her' by her voice.[raizel.winCount 0 2 | You could beseech her for mercy on future crossings. If it's not obvious by now, you're not much a threat to her. You've [raizel.winCount 0 1 |never |rarely ] won a fight against her, and it's starting to hurt – and make you afraid for future crossings. You don't know what you did, but you just want to be left alone. | After the numerous attempts she's made to defeat you, you've [raizel.winCount 3 5 |come out on top more often than you haven't |never lost ], despite her repeated attempts at opportunism and underhandedness. You don't know why she's doing it, but it's starting to get tiresome, and you're starting to feel a little bad for her. You presume that she's doing it out of desperation, and maybe reasoning with her that violence – at least, towards you – isn't the answer. ][pc.bgMulti hunter slumrat | Thanks to your history as a hunter in the cold wilderness, you recognize her tactics: she laid in wait, saw an opportunity to strike, and she struck. However, her techniques are sloppy and unfocused, relying on speed and brute force, which is why it's never worked on you. Your advice would be unsolicited, and you'd have to ask her to stop using it on travelers, but maybe giving her some pointers on how to hunt more effectively could get you in her good graces. | You've lived in the slums for most of your life. You know what it's like to lie in wait for an easy mark to take advantage of, because a successful mark was often the difference between dinner and starving. From the way she moves, she's probably lived her whole life in the shadows, outcast from society, just like you. You're not going to pretend that you're ‘better' than her[raizel.winCount 0 2 |, especially since she kept winning |, especially after you kept beating her ], but... maybe bonding with a kindred spirit could help you and her come to some sort of understanding. ]
rows.translation: 这是一片未知的领域，但你还是决定抓住这个机会，朝着那栋你看到那个生物溜进去的建筑走去。这一次，情况有所不同…… 你 打扰 它你根本无法想象这件事最终会如何发展，但是…… [raizel.winCount 0 2 |如果它在有机会的时候没有攻击你——尽管在街道这种开阔的环境中，它无法偷偷地攻击你——那么你就会希望它这次也不会再攻击你。 |既然它在有机会攻击你的时候并没有这么做，那么它应该已经明白，使用暴力是没有意义的。当然，它仍然可能会为了保护自己的巢穴而发起攻击，但如果是这样的话，你只会选择撤退，而它也会从中吸取教训。 ]你穿过这座建筑唯一的一扇门框——那扇门本身还挂在门轴上，但看起来已经很久没有被人打开或关闭过了——然后向里面的黑暗中望去。“喂？”你对着那片黑暗喊道。 起初，没有任何反应。 然后，一对宝石般红润的眼睛出现了——那轻型芒如此强烈，仿佛能够穿透一切障碍。它们似乎是从虚无中突然浮现出来的。当那双眼睛睁开时，它们的视线立刻锁定在了你身上，仿佛从一开始就在注视着你一样。 目轻型在视线的高度相遇[pc.heightRange 0 84 | |我想告诉你，无论那是什么，它的高度都非常惊人。 ]在黑暗中，你根本看不到它的其他部分——无论它身上穿着什么，它的伪装效果都非常好。[raizel.winCount 0 2 |你想要什么？”它问道。 |走开，”它轻蔑地说道。 ]从它的声音来看，属于女性嗓音，不过音调较低，听起来有些粗哑。这种声音通常会出现在那些环境不太好的酒吧里，是那种有些人可能会经常轻型顾的地方。至少，你并不是在追捕某种动物。 你有几种方式可以选择来回应她。 第一种方式是最简单、最直接的方法：你就告诉她，你只是想和她聊聊。她已经多次攻击你，而你真正想知道的，只是为什么。 简化处理或许是一种更容易接受它的方法。你……你是从她的声音中判断出她是一个“她”吧？[raizel.winCount 0 2 | 在未来再次与她相遇时，你可以恳求她宽恕你。如果到现在她还没有意识到这一点，那就说明你对她来说并没有太大的威胁……你确实如此。 [raizel.winCount 0 1 |永远不会 |很少 ] 与她的一场争斗让你深受伤害，这种痛苦让你开始害怕未来的任何冲突。你并不清楚自己究竟做了什么，只希望能被人放过，安静地生活。 | 在她多次尝试击败你的过程中，你…… [raizel.winCount 3 5 |更多时候，你都能取得胜利。 |从未失败过 ]尽管她屡次试图采取机会主义和阴险的手段，但你并不明白她为何要这样做。这种行为渐渐让人感到厌烦，你甚至开始为她感到有些同情。你认为她之所以这样做，是因为走投无路了，或许试着跟她讲道理，告诉她——至少对她来说——使用暴力并不是解决问题的办法。 ][pc.bgMulti hunter slumrat | 由于你曾在寒冷的荒野中担任猎人的经历，你能够识破她的战术：她潜伏等待，一旦发现机会就会立即出击。然而，她的技巧粗糙且缺乏针对性，完全依赖速度和蛮力，因此这些手段从来都对你不奏效。你或许可以主动建议她不要再对旅行者使用这种手段，但或许给她一些关于如何更有效地狩猎的建议，反而能赢得她的好感。 | 你大半生都生活在贫民窟里。你知道那种等待机会来占别人便宜的感觉——因为能否抓住这样的机会，往往就意味着能否吃上饭或者挨饿。从她的举止来看，她很可能也像你一样，一生都在社会的阴影中度过，被排斥在正常的社会生活之外。你总不可能假装自己比她“优越”吧。[raizel.winCount 0 2 |尤其是她屡次获胜之后，这种情况更加明显了。 |尤其是在你一次次击败她之后…… ]但是……也许与一个志同道合的人建立联系，能够帮助你和她达成某种理解。 ]
rows.raw: " This is uncharted territory, but you take the chance and make your way towards the one building that you watched the creature slip into. This time, it's you intruding on it. You can't begin to guess how this is going to go, but [raizel.winCount 0 2 |if it didn't attack you when it had the chance – albeit, in the more broad ‘light' of the street, where it couldn't sneak-attack you – then you want to believe that it won't attack you again this time |given that it didn't attack you when it could have, it's come to understand that violence isn't worthwhile. Then again, it might still lash out to protect its nest, but if that's the case, you'll retreat, and your lesson will be learned ]. You cross the threshold from the building's only doorframe – the door itself still on the hinges, but it looks like it hasn't opened or closed in an age – and peer into its darkness. "Hello?" you call into the abyss. At first, no response. Then, a pair of ruby-red eyes, bright enough to pierce the veil. They materialize into being from seemingly nothing at all. As soon as they open, they focus directly onto you, as if they had been watching you from the very start. The eyes meet you at eye-level[pc.heightRange 0 84 | |, telling you that, whatever it is, it's very tall ]. You can't see any other part of it in the darkness – whatever it's wearing, the camouflage is very well done. "[raizel.winCount 0 2 |What do you want?" it asks. |Go away," it says disdainfully ]. From the sound of its voice, it's feminine, albeit on the lower, gruffer side. It's the kind of voice that you'd hear at a seedier, less reputable bar, one that someone might frequent a little too often. At least you're not chasing some animal. You have a few options on how you want to respond. The first is the easiest, simplest, and straightest way forward: you tell her that you just want to talk. She's assailed you several times and all you want to know is why. Keeping it simple could be an easy way to open up to it. It? You presume she's a ‘her' by her voice.[raizel.winCount 0 2 | You could beseech her for mercy on future crossings. If it's not obvious by now, you're not much a threat to her. You've [raizel.winCount 0 1 |never |rarely ] won a fight against her, and it's starting to hurt – and make you afraid for future crossings. You don't know what you did, but you just want to be left alone. | After the numerous attempts she's made to defeat you, you've [raizel.winCount 3 5 |come out on top more often than you haven't |never lost ], despite her repeated attempts at opportunism and underhandedness. You don't know why she's doing it, but it's starting to get tiresome, and you're starting to feel a little bad for her. You presume that she's doing it out of desperation, and maybe reasoning with her that violence – at least, towards you – isn't the answer. ][pc.bgMulti hunter slumrat | Thanks to your history as a hunter in the cold wilderness, you recognize her tactics: she laid in wait, saw an opportunity to strike, and she struck. However, her techniques are sloppy and unfocused, relying on speed and brute force, which is why it's never worked on you. Your advice would be unsolicited, and you'd have to ask her to stop using it on travelers, but maybe giving her some pointers on how to hunt more effectively could get you in her good graces. | You've lived in the slums for most of your life. You know what it's like to lie in wait for an easy mark to take advantage of, because a successful mark was often the difference between dinner and starving. From the way she moves, she's probably lived her whole life in the shadows, outcast from society, just like you. You're not going to pretend that you're ‘better' than her[raizel.winCount 0 2 |, especially since she kept winning |, especially after you kept beating her ], but... maybe bonding with a kindred spirit could help you and her come to some sort of understanding. ] "

rows.original: [var0 |You're not going to pretend you're friends. From the way her eyes drill holes into you, and from the tone of her voice, she's not in the mood to entertain guests, either. Keeping things curt and to-the-point may be the healthiest option. You ask her why she attacked you, and why she kept attacking you: if you knew the reason why, maybe you could avoid making her so antagonistic in the future. |You tell her that... look. You're clearly not much of a fighter, at least when it comes to her. You've [raizel.winCount 0 1 |never |rarely ] beaten her, and you're thankful for the mercy she's shown you by letting you live every time. All you want is for her to... stop. You're not a threat. You can't win. You don't know what you did to make her angry, but you just want to cross in peace. At first, there's no response. The ruby-red eyes hover in the darkness, fixated on you. They could lunge at any moment, and you'd be at an even worse disadvantage than if she had just jumped you on the street. You're tense, and you think she can see that. "Quit your groveling," she says eventually. "It's sad. If you can't fight to save your life, at least learn how to beg for it properly." ... Does that mean she wants you to beg her to stop? She sighs. "I'm not gonna hurt'cha," she replies. "There's nothing of yours that I want anymore. If that's all you're worried about, hurry up and leave." You put one foot behind the other, initially thinking of leaving her abode, but... now, you're curious. You ask her why she attacked you at all, if she's just going to let you go like that. |You came here to suggest to her that... well, she doesn't need you to point out the obvious, but trying to get the jump on you hasn't worked out for her. You're a seasoned combatant at this point, and her tactics are repetitive. You're not here to gloat, but you are here to suggest that she ought to quit while she's ahead. Eventually, she's going to jump someone that's better than her, and they're not going to stop at just winning the fight. "Go fuck yourself," she says venomously. Her red eyes narrow into accusatory slits. More than the vitriol, you can hear the frustration in her tone. She knows that she's lost against you a handful of times and you reminding her of it is little more than salt in the wound. "Spoken like someone that's never had to fight for their right to live. Have you considered that going after you wasn't something I wanted, either?" Okay, maybe choosing this line of thought wasn't the wisest route you could have taken. You ask her, then, if she never ‘wanted' to attack you, then why did she keep doing it, even after it was clear that you weren't an easy mark? Her situation is clearly desperate, but... how desperate? |You tell her that you're a hunter by trade. You spend a lot of time in the wilderness, hunting all manner of game, big or small. You recognize a lot of her techniques – she has the makings of a hunter herself, if she wanted. "Not interested," she answers quickly and sternly. Okay, if she doesn't want to take up an honest hunting, then... what if you taught her about hunting dishonestly? Her ruby-red eyes, glowing through the darkness, narrow in thought, confusion, and weariness. "What the hell does that mean?" Take it from a professional: her technique is sloppy, relying on speed and brute force. She's striking in the dark of the cave, where the terrain favors her, and those are smart decisions, but there's more to bagging her target than choosing her venue. You could teach her some of the tricks you're learned over your life, if she wants. There's a long pause as she considers your answer. Her red eyes sway in the darkness slightly, tilting to one side, as if she's leaning her head onto her hand in thought. She doesn't blink – and you realize that she hasn't since you started speaking with her. "What's in it for you?" she asks. "Nothing is ever free." Well, you can't make her promise to not use it to kill anyone[raizel.winCount 0 5 |. Not that you think that she would: she's had the opportunity to kill you, and she didn't take it, leading you to believe that she isn't a killer ]. Even if she did promise, you doubt she'd keep her word. Instead, you ask for knowledge in return for knowledge. "I don't know [silly |shit about fuck |nothin' ]," she replies. No, there's one thing. You want to know why she attacked you. And you want to know why she kept doing it. |You look over the abode that she's made for herself. You can't see a lot, thanks to the poor lighting of the Undermountain, but you recognize the place by its feel, not by its visuals. It's shitty, it's dirty, it's dark, it's cold. There's mold all over the place. What organic material you can see is rotten; any fabric, like her bedroll, is torn. It's like home. Her ruby-red eyes widen, very slightly. Anyone else would have missed it, but you, living your life, you've come to recognize even the minutest change in a person's expression, even if all you can see is their eyes. "Home?" she repeats. Yeah. You get it. You know what it's like to live like a rat, scurrying from one place to call ‘home' to another. How you couldn't afford to keep friends because the only ‘friends' available to people like you, were people like you, forced to lie and cheat and steal to survive. A generous society would rather brush you into some dark corner and not have to look at you, saying that scum like you lower the ‘aesthetics'. More than once, they tried to kill you just because you lived in their gutters. Not with a sword or with magic, but by denying you the most basic courtesy of letting you sleep in a hole you dug with your own hands to keep warm from the cold. Her red eyes widen even further, and their ridges curve sympathetically. "Oh my God, you do get it," she says wistfully. "Nobody's ever put it to words like that." You're doing well enough for yourself lately that you've earned the privilege of traveling between Hawkethorne and Khor'minos, among other things. But, just like how it is [silly |in this bitch of a world |in life ], you got your start purely through happenstance, through knowing someone important and by being in the right place at the right time. "Right?!" she asks as her eyes lean backward. "It doesn't matter what my skills are. What matters is that I'm dirty and I frighten small children. Nobody cares about what we can do, they only care about who we are, and sometimes, who we are, is ‘lucky'." Perfect: you've established some common ground. You tell her that you're not here to rob her, or to fight. You're not naïve enough to think that you two are about to be friends, not after what you just said about how hard it is to make them. You're just here to ask her one question: why is it that she kept coming after you? You could make an educated guess, but [raizel.winCount 0 4 |when she had the opportunity to kill you, she didn't take it, and when she won, she could have stolen your every coin, but she didn't. You're just... curious. |she never once beat you in an altercation, yet she kept trying. Her situation must be especially desperate. Something that you relate to, but not to the level she's demonstrated. You're just... curious. ] ] She leans forward, her eyes closing the gap between you and her. She's close enough that she could lunge and close the distance in a blink, if she wanted – a posture and distance that feels all-too-familiar with her at this point. "‘Cause I wanted to eat'cha," she says lowly. You can hear the saliva in her jowls as she speaks. "I was gonna crush you until your bones were mush, then I was gonna swallow you whole, from your head to your feet. Nobody would ever find you. You'd feed me for weeks." [raizel.winCount 0 1 |She had at least one opportunity, where she had you unconscious and vulnerable, and yet here you are, uneaten. "Yeah, well, I decided that I wasn't in the mood for [pc.race]," she answers flippantly. |Well, then, you'll have to apologize for not giving her the opportunity to have a decent meal. "I took it easy on you every time," she answers flippantly. "Lucky for you, [pc.race] doesn't agree with me." ] You ask her for a serious answer. "[pc.bg slumrat |Come on, why do you think? ]I wanted your money, stupid. I saw some fool walking somewhere they weren't suppose'ta, figured someone that got past them minotaurs must be some bigwig, bigwigs usually got money, and I wanted your money. [raizel.winCount 0 2 |Eventually, I started getting bored and you started getting pathetic. It was like punching a puppy. People think I'm a monster, but I'm not a monster. There's only so much puppy-punching I can do. |And then you turned out to be too much effort for an easy mark. It's easier to rob someone when they don't got a clue how to handle themselves, and unfortunately for me, you got an idea or two. People like to think that I'm some dumb monster, but I'm not a dumb monster. I know when I'm beat. ]" Does that mean she's going to stop attacking you on the road? [raizel.winCount 0 2 |Out of some sense of mercy? |Because you're not worth the effort? ] "[var0 |Y |Like I told you, y |Y |Y |Y ]ou don't have to worry about me stepping on your toes anymore, [pc.race]," she says. Then, her red eyes narrow, taking a more frustrated and direct look. "Now, I answered your questions.[var0 |" |" |" |You promised me how to hunt dirty. It's your turn." You suppose you did. |" ]
rows.translation: [var0 |你总不可能装作我们是朋友吧。从她那直勾勾盯着你的眼神，以及她说话的语气来看，她现在也根本没有心情招待客人。保持简短直接的态度，或许才是最明智的选择。你问她为什么攻击你，为什么一直攻击你——如果你知道了原因，也许将来就能避免让她变得如此敌对了。 |你告诉她……听着，很明显，你在和她对抗的时候根本不是她的对手。你根本…… [raizel.winCount 0 1 |永远不会 |很少 ] 你伤害了她，而每次她都能宽恕你，让你活下来，你对此心存感激。你只希望她……能停止这一切。你根本不是她的威胁，你也赢不了。你不知道自己做了什么才惹她生气，但你只是想平静地生活下去。 起初，没有任何反应。那双红宝石般的眼睛在暗影中凝视着你，仿佛随时都会扑上来。那样的话，你的处境将会比她在街上突然袭击你时还要糟糕。你感到紧张，而且你认为她也能看出这一点。 别再这种卑躬屈膝的样子了，”她最终说道，“真让人难看。如果你连为自己而战都做不到，至少要学会如何好好地乞求吧。” ……这是不是意味着她希望你求她停止这样做？ 她叹了口气。 我不会伤害你的，”她回答道，“我已经不再想要你的任何东西了。如果你只是担心这个，那就快离开吧。” 你一步步地走出了她的住所，起初确实打算离开那里，但是……现在，你好奇了。你问她，既然她本来打算就这样放你走，那为什么还要攻击你呢？ |你来到这里，是想告诉她……嗯，她其实并不需要你去指出那些显而易见的事情，但她试图先发制人这个策略并没有奏效。你现在已经是一个经验丰富的“战斗者”了，而她的手部段实在太老套了。你来到这里并不是为了炫耀，而是为了…… 是 我建议她趁现在还有机会赶紧退出吧。迟早她会遇到比她更强的人，而那些人可不会仅仅满足于赢得一场战斗而已。 “去死吧，”她恶毒地说道。 她的红眼睛眯成充满指责的细缝。从她的语气中，不仅能听到怨恨，还能感受到沮丧。她知道自己已经多次输给了你，而你提醒她这一点，无异于在她的伤口上撒盐。 这话听起来就像是一个从来不需要为生存权而抗争的人说的。你有没有想过，那些追捕你的人，他们这么做其实也是有原因的…… 我 难道她从来就没有想要攻击你的念头吗？” 好吧，也许选择这种思考方式并不是最明智的做法。 那么你可以问问她：如果她从来就没有想要攻击你的想法，那么为什么在明明知道你并不是一个容易对付的目标之后，她还是继续这样做呢？她的处境显然很绝望，但是…… 如何 绝望了吗？ |你告诉她，你的职业是猎人。你大部分时间都在荒野中度过，猎捕各种大小的猎物。你注意到她使用了很多狩猎技巧——如果她愿意的话，她本身也完全有成为猎人的潜力。 没有兴趣，”她迅速而坚定地回答。 好吧，如果她不愿意从事诚实的狩猎活动，那么……如果你教她如何通过不正当手部段进行狩猎，会怎么样呢？ 她那宝石般红润的眼睛在暗影中闪烁着光芒，此时她的目光因思考、困惑与疲惫而变得眯了起来。 这到底是什么意思？” 听一个专业人士的说法：她的技巧很粗糙，完全依靠速度和蛮力。她在洞穴的暗影环境中发动攻击，而那里的地形对她有利，这些选择确实很明智，但要想成功击中目标，仅仅选择合适的地点是不够的。 如果她愿意的话，你可以把她教会一些你这些年来学到的技巧。 她仔细考虑着你的回答，沉默了很长时间。在暗影中，她那双红色的眼睛微微晃动，偏向了一侧，仿佛她正用手部托着头陷入沉思之中。 她没有眨眼——你意识到，自从你开始和她交谈以来，她就一直没有眨过眼。“这对你有什么好处？”她问道，“没有什么是免费的。” 嗯，你无法强迫她承诺不会用它来伤害别人。[raizel.winCount 0 5 |. 其实你也不觉得她会那么做：她本来就有机会杀人的。 你她没有接受它，这让你们以为她并不是一个杀人犯。 ]. 即使她真的做出了承诺，你也不相信她会遵守。因此，你选择用知识来换取知识。 “我不知道。 [silly |胡闹一番 |没什么 ]不是这样的，”她回答道。 “其实有件事。你想知道她为什么攻击你，也想知道她为什么一直这样做。 rows.raw: " [var0 |You're not going to pretend you're friends. From the way her eyes drill holes into you, and from the tone of her voice, she's not in the mood to entertain guests, either. Keeping things curt and to-the-point may be the healthiest option. You ask her why she attacked you, and why she kept attacking you: if you knew the reason why, maybe you could avoid making her so antagonistic in the future. |You tell her that... look. You're clearly not much of a fighter, at least when it comes to her. You've [raizel.winCount 0 1 |never |rarely ] beaten her, and you're thankful for the mercy she's shown you by letting you live every time. All you want is for her to... stop. You're not a threat. You can't win. You don't know what you did to make her angry, but you just want to cross in peace. At first, there's no response. The ruby-red eyes hover in the darkness, fixated on you. They could lunge at any moment, and you'd be at an even worse disadvantage than if she had just jumped you on the street. You're tense, and you think she can see that. "Quit your groveling," she says eventually. "It's sad. If you can't fight to save your life, at least learn how to beg for it properly." ... Does that mean she wants you to beg her to stop? She sighs. "I'm not gonna hurt'cha," she replies. "There's nothing of yours that I want anymore. If that's all you're worried about, hurry up and leave." You put one foot behind the other, initially thinking of leaving her abode, but... now, you're curious. You ask her why she attacked you at all, if she's just going to let you go like that. |You came here to suggest to her that... well, she doesn't need you to point out the obvious, but trying to get the jump on you hasn't worked out for her. You're a seasoned combatant at this point, and her tactics are repetitive. You're not here to gloat, but you are here to suggest that she ought to quit while she's ahead. Eventually, she's going to jump someone that's better than her, and they're not going to stop at just winning the fight. "Go fuck yourself," she says venomously. Her red eyes narrow into accusatory slits. More than the vitriol, you can hear the frustration in her tone. She knows that she's lost against you a handful of times and you reminding her of it is little more than salt in the wound. "Spoken like someone that's never had to fight for their right to live. Have you considered that going after you wasn't something I wanted, either?" Okay, maybe choosing this line of thought wasn't the wisest route you could have taken. You ask her, then, if she never ‘wanted' to attack you, then why did she keep doing it, even after it was clear that you weren't an easy mark? Her situation is clearly desperate, but... how desperate? |You tell her that you're a hunter by trade. You spend a lot of time in the wilderness, hunting all manner of game, big or small. You recognize a lot of her techniques – she has the makings of a hunter herself, if she wanted. "Not interested," she answers quickly and sternly. Okay, if she doesn't want to take up an honest hunting, then... what if you taught her about hunting dishonestly? Her ruby-red eyes, glowing through the darkness, narrow in thought, confusion, and weariness. "What the hell does that mean?" Take it from a professional: her technique is sloppy, relying on speed and brute force. She's striking in the dark of the cave, where the terrain favors her, and those are smart decisions, but there's more to bagging her target than choosing her venue. You could teach her some of the tricks you're learned over your life, if she wants. There's a long pause as she considers your answer. Her red eyes sway in the darkness slightly, tilting to one side, as if she's leaning her head onto her hand in thought. She doesn't blink – and you realize that she hasn't since you started speaking with her. "What's in it for you?" she asks. "Nothing is ever free." Well, you can't make her promise to not use it to kill anyone[raizel.winCount 0 5 |. Not that you think that she would: she's had the opportunity to kill you, and she didn't take it, leading you to believe that she isn't a killer ]. Even if she did promise, you doubt she'd keep her word. Instead, you ask for knowledge in return for knowledge. "I don't know [silly |shit about fuck |nothin' ]," she replies. No, there's one thing. You want to know why she attacked you. And you want to know why she kept doing it. |You look over the abode that she's made for herself. You can't see a lot, thanks to the poor lighting of the Undermountain, but you recognize the place by its feel, not by its visuals. It's shitty, it's dirty, it's dark, it's cold. There's mold all over the place. What organic material you can see is rotten; any fabric, like her bedroll, is torn. It's like home. Her ruby-red eyes widen, very slightly. Anyone else would have missed it, but you, living your life, you've come to recognize even the minutest change in a person's expression, even if all you can see is their eyes. "Home?" she repeats. Yeah. You get it. You know what it's like to live like a rat, scurrying from one place to call ‘home' to another. How you couldn't afford to keep friends because the only ‘friends' available to people like you, were people like you, forced to lie and cheat and steal to survive. A generous society would rather brush you into some dark corner and not have to look at you, saying that scum like you lower the ‘aesthetics'. More than once, they tried to kill you just because you lived in their gutters. Not with a sword or with magic, but by denying you the most basic courtesy of letting you sleep in a hole you dug with your own hands to keep warm from the cold. Her red eyes widen even further, and their ridges curve sympathetically. "Oh my God, you do get it," she says wistfully. "Nobody's ever put it to words like that." You're doing well enough for yourself lately that you've earned the privilege of traveling between Hawkethorne and Khor'minos, among other things. But, just like how it is [silly |in this bitch of a world |in life ], you got your start purely through happenstance, through knowing someone important and by being in the right place at the right time. "Right?!" she asks as her eyes lean backward. "It doesn't matter what my skills are. What matters is that I'm dirty and I frighten small children. Nobody cares about what we can do, they only care about who we are, and sometimes, who we are, is ‘lucky'." Perfect: you've established some common ground. You tell her that you're not here to rob her, or to fight. You're not naïve enough to think that you two are about to be friends, not after what you just said about how hard it is to make them. You're just here to ask her one question: why is it that she kept coming after you? You could make an educated guess, but [raizel.winCount 0 4 |when she had the opportunity to kill you, she didn't take it, and when she won, she could have stolen your every coin, but she didn't. You're just... curious. |she never once beat you in an altercation, yet she kept trying. Her situation must be especially desperate. Something that you relate to, but not to the level she's demonstrated. You're just... curious. ] ] She leans forward, her eyes closing the gap between you and her. She's close enough that she could lunge and close the distance in a blink, if she wanted – a posture and distance that feels all-too-familiar with her at this point. "‘Cause I wanted to eat'cha," she says lowly. You can hear the saliva in her jowls as she speaks. "I was gonna crush you until your bones were mush, then I was gonna swallow you whole, from your head to your feet. Nobody would ever find you. You'd feed me for weeks." [raizel.winCount 0 1 |She had at least one opportunity, where she had you unconscious and vulnerable, and yet here you are, uneaten. "Yeah, well, I decided that I wasn't in the mood for [pc.race]," she answers flippantly. |Well, then, you'll have to apologize for not giving her the opportunity to have a decent meal. "I took it easy on you every time," she answers flippantly. "Lucky for you, [pc.race] doesn't agree with me." ] You ask her for a serious answer. "[pc.bg slumrat |Come on, why do you think? ]I wanted your money, stupid. I saw some fool walking somewhere they weren't suppose'ta, figured someone that got past them minotaurs must be some bigwig, bigwigs usually got money, and I wanted your money. [raizel.winCount 0 2 |Eventually, I started getting bored and you started getting pathetic. It was like punching a puppy. People think I'm a monster, but I'm not a monster. There's only so much puppy-punching I can do. |And then you turned out to be too much effort for an easy mark. It's easier to rob someone when they don't got a clue how to handle themselves, and unfortunately for me, you got an idea or two. People like to think that I'm some dumb monster, but I'm not a dumb monster. I know when I'm beat. ]" Does that mean she's going to stop attacking you on the road? [raizel.winCount 0 2 |Out of some sense of mercy? |Because you're not worth the effort? ] "[var0 |Y |Like I told you, y |Y |Y |Y ]ou don't have to worry about me stepping on your toes anymore, [pc.race]," she says. Then, her red eyes narrow, taking a more frustrated and direct look. "Now, I answered your questions.[var0 |" |" |" |You promised me how to hunt dirty. It's your turn." You suppose you did. |" ] "

rows.original: [var1 |You know everything there is to being a hunter, hunting large and small game, and everything you know could be applied to taking down something smarter. But because you know all that, you also know how to lie about knowing what you know. ]You reiterate that she had a lot of the ‘basics' down, namely, only choosing to strike when the circumstances were strongly in her favor. Going from there, you explain some of the more effective techniques you use in trapping prey: [var1 |for example, especially in a place with as little foot traffic as this side of the Undermountain, it's important to adjust your stakeout point every now and again to find new prey to focus down. While bait can be useful to attract targets, it can also be used to repel them: if you put something repellent somewhere you think a target is going to be and drive them away from it, that can make them easier to take down in terrain that they aren't used to |everything from wearing them down by stalking them over a longer distance, to setting out bait or other distractions to make your strike more effective. It's not about force: the fewer moves you need to make, the better your odds at being successful ]. To you, it's also basic stuff. Using traps, laying bait, it's pretty standard for a hunter like you. But, thankfully, your shrouded-in-shadow conversation partner is attentive, absorbing everything you say with rapt attention. "Not a whole lot to use for ‘bait' here in the caves," she notes. Bait doesn't necessarily have to be food. [var1 |Anything ‘repellent' could be anything from poisonous fungus to something visually unpleasant. If she can handle it, manure works great. |It can be anything that might pique a target's attention. Something shiny. A rhythmic, unnatural noise. Hell, she herself could try crying for help. ] After you finish your lessons, she pauses, her eyes narrowed on you once more, trying to decide for herself if you're being trustworthy. "You know I'm going to use all this information to mug people, right?" she asks. Yes, you know that. But you're not concerned with if she ‘mugs' people. [raizel.winCount 0 2 |She had the opportunity to kill you, and she didn't take it, which tells you that she's not looking to kill. Which also tells you that her story about fighting you for your money is honest. |Even if she was a good enough fighter to take you down consistently, you don't think she's a killer: her lifestyle is too conspicuous. You know she isn't moving from her spot. If people started going missing from this area of the Undermountain, it'd be easy to find her. ] She hums. "Well. We're done here. Unless you're looking to get fucked six ways to stupid, I'm going to ask you[raizel.winCount 0 2 | | again ] to leave." [pc.isBimbo |What's this now? Nobody said anything about getting fucked six ways to stupid. You didn't even know there were six ways to get fucked stupid! You're only familiar with, uhh... three. Maybe four. But six? Now we're talking! You should ask about getting fucked six ways to stupid! |[pc.bg courtesan |... Coming from your work as an escort, you recognize that odd and sudden turn-of-phrase and the tone that she used. A part of her is hoping that you'd take her up on her offer, but she's masking her fear of rejection by saying it aggressively – after all, if she's mean about it, that's the reason why you'd say no, and not any other reason.
